title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: Birding at Lake Junaluska
description:
Birding at Lake Junaluska
with Shane Myers 
Saturday, November 14  |  8 am – 12 pm 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
Fall is a great time to go looking for ducks and other migratory waterbirds. Let’s go walk around Lake Junaluska and see what birds are using the lake as a stopping point on their way south! 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Shane Myers’ interest in nature began as a child with a love of dinosaurs. This quickly grew to include fossils, insects, and reptiles, and learning from the notes his grandparents kept of the birds that came to their feeders in Toledo, Ohio.  He has a Bachelors of Science in Wildlife Biology and did most of his undergraduate work on dragonflies and damselflies. He’s assisted in outreach and education for plant conservation groups, Odonata Groups, and various bird groups. Shane currently works for the Adult Education department at the NC Arboretum.

title: Scenic Avl Series #1: Hard Times Trail - Arboretum
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
If you plan to carpool, add a comment below.

Join me for a hike in Bent Creek. We will start at the Hard Times trailhead and hike about 6 miles. We will stop to see the exhibit in the visitors center in the Arboretum - 20 minutes.

title: Choose Between a 5 KM/3.1 Mile and a 10 KM/6.2 Mile Guided Waynesville Walk
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
We will be joining the Asheville Amblers, AARP, the Cardinals Elite Walking Team, and perhaps some others for this event. Registration is at 9:30 a.m. with step-off at 10:00. The walk is free, although the Amblers do accept donations (suggested donation $4.00).

Meet in front of Mast General Store, 63 N. Main St., Waynesville NC 28786. The walks go past public art, Civil War sites, along the Waynesville Greenway, and more. The 10 KM walk adds Town Hall, the historic Frog Level area, nice neighborhoods, and a peaceful cemetery with spectacular views.

Note: the 5 KM walk will be at a slightly slower pace. The 10 KM walk will be at a slightly faster pace.

There are some hills, so some may want walking poles (I will be taking both of mine); sneakers should be fine. Dogs are welcome. Strollers should be ok, though it will require one or two work-arounds. Bring plenty of water and a protein snack. Dress appropriately for the weather.

Parking is easier a block to either side of Main Street. Mast General Store doesn't have a public restroom, but we can direct you to one nearby should you need it.

Many people go out to eat together after this walk at places like Sweet Onion and Angelos. You will want to shop at Mast General Store and several other downtown shops. The last time we did this walk, people were asking about the availability of ice cream and chocolates.

Why not make a day of it!

All levels are welcome. Please bring your own yoga mat. No mat, no problem, the Museum has some extra mats to lend. Loose-fitting clothing is recommended, ensuring ease of movement as you flow through your practice.

title: Jazz Brunch w/ “Four Peanuts” trio
location: French Broad River Brewery, 101 Fairview Rd, Asheville, NC, United States
description:
Jazz Brunch is now officially on the schedule for every Saturday here in the taproom! We’re so very excited to introduce our newest free weekly event, open to all ages, family & pet-friendly





If you haven’t experienced Jazz Brunch yet, here’s what you can expect: from the moment the music begins, the taproom fills with that perfect weekend energy… laid-back jazz, fresh brunch plates, great beer, and a room full of people settling in and staying awhile. Friends gather around tables, conversations flow easily, and the rhythm of the music sets the tone for a perfect, easy Saturday. It’s exactly the kind of atmosphere we hoped to create when this idea first came to life!



We’re especially excited to continue working with our house Jazz band, “Four Peanuts”, whose smooth, soulful sound brings everything together. The group explores both original compositions and zesty covers of tunes you may or may not know. The trio features Alex Taub on keyboards, Brennan Dugan on bass, and Joe Enright on drums, and will certainly leave your peanuts salted and boiled to perfection! Their music pairs effortlessly with the relaxed brunch setting, turning an ordinary morning into something memorable. The all-new brunch menu is absolutely something to be excited about! French Broad River Pizza will be serving up a mix of breakfast and lunch favorites designed to pair perfectly with a chill afternoon in the taproom.






Thank you for supporting live music, local artists, and community gatherings here at French Broad River Brewery. We can’t wait to welcome you back to the taproom… brunch plate in one hand, beer in the other, and jazz in the background.


  
French Broad River Brewery is more than just a place to enjoy a drink—it’s a community hub where great beer, delicious pizza, live music, and good times come together. Just minutes from the Biltmore Estate & Downtown, our taproom is a gathering spot for locals and visitors alike. We regularly host live music and entertainment in our taproom, making French Broad River Brewery a lively hub of local activity. From bluegrass to reggae, there’s always something happening. Check out our Events Page to see what’s coming up next! 
No brewery experience is complete without great food. That’s why we offer French Broad River Pizza, serving up hot, hand-tossed pizzas made to order. Whether you’re here for a quick slice or a full meal, our pizza perfectly complements our craft beers and the lively atmosphere of our taproom. frenchbroadbrewery.com/pizza

title: Floating Action Live at The Mule
description:
One of Asheville’s best-kept musical secrets is coming to The Mule
Floating Action is the Black Mountain project Seth Kauffman started in 2005, after his Motown-soaked group The Choosy Beggars called it quits. Seth writes the songs, writes the lyrics, plays nearly every instrument, and records and produces it all himself. The result is homemade psychedelic pop with a lot of heart: warm, strange, and crafted by someone who cares more about getting the song right than getting famous.

That devotion hasn’t gone unnoticed. Jim James of My Morning Jacket has called him “the most underrated person in music.” Seth has lent his guitar, bass, and drums to records by Lana Del Rey, Angel Olsen, Ray LaMontagne, and Jim James, and the Asheville scene has long considered him one of its own. Floating Action has played South by Southwest and the Hangout Music Festival, and on November 14 he’s playing our taproom. 
The name says plenty about him: it comes from an out-of-date Gretsch kick-drum pedal. It’s a small, scrappy piece of gear that became the name of a band worth knowing. 
Come early, grab a seat, and spend a Saturday afternoon with one of the area’s great underrated songwriters. 
FREE. All ages welcome.

title: Chase the Rising Sun - Ecstatic Dance Waves w/ Rory Jagdeo
description:
Asheville Movement Collective
Sunday, November 15th
1st Dance Wave 8:30\-10:30am \| Warmup 8:30am \| Opening Circle 9am
2nd Dance Wave 10:30\-12:30am \| Warmup 10:30am \| Opening Circle 11am
Facilitator Rory Jagdeo

Intention: Chase the Rising Sun

**RISE AND SET\~ Anonymous**

Sunrise, all so bright
A new start for my life
Fresh skin, new eyes
Awake beneath the endless skies

Nature’s beauty, whisper of trees
A fleeting gift upon the breeze

Enjoy it now, it won’t stay
There is sunset that always comes again
Light fades—darkness whispers its place
Symbol of decay comes every day

Still sunrise, no surprise
Leaving lessons deep inside
Remember—change to shine

But still, it sets again
Light fades and dawn returns again
The sun never stay the same

## About Rory Jagdeo

Rory is a singer/songwriter and an AMC Facilitator. He stepped into Ecstatic Dance in Houston, TX for the first time in 2014 and believes in the power of dance to transform and bring a healthier, happier, and connected lifestyle. It is that driving force and passion that pushes him to explore the role of being an Ecstatic Dance Facilitator using world rhythms and different musical genres to weave mixes that incorporate many elements of 8Rhythms.

title: John Rock Loop Hike
description:
WNC Sierra Club
Join the WNC Sierra Club for a beautiful hike in the Pisgah National Forest. The John Rock Loop hike features around 1,100 feet of elevation gain up to a scenic overlook where we will have a snack and rest. This hike is about 5.9 miles in length and will take us approximately 3-4 hours. Be prepared for elevation gain and creek crossings. Make sure to pack food and water to stay nourished and hydrated! Wear gear that you are comfortable hiking in and good shoes. It is also a good idea to have rain gear just to be safe. If you are feeling unwell and/or have a fever, please help us to keep everyone safe and healthy by waiting for the next outing. Families, friends, and pets are all welcome. An adult must accompany all children. All dogs must remain on a leash and be friendly to all.

Please arrive a few minutes early to say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.

ABOUT THE MUSICIAN
Diego Vázquez is a Spanish pianist from Madrid now based in Asheville who views music as a way to understand and express emotions beyond words. He began playing at age four and developed a strong classical foundation, later expanding into pop and musical theater. After years of studying in Spain, he now pursues music independently in the United States, performing as a chapel pianist, choir member, and orchestra musician while also learning the organ. title: The Body of the Golem: A Life in Portraiture
description:
Artist and writer Riva Lehrer brings together portraiture, Jewish tradition, disability, and the figure of the golem for the 2026 Phyllis Freed Sollod Memorial Lecture in the Mountain View Room of the Sherrill Center. Through art and storytelling, Lehrer explores who gets labeled “monstrous,” who has the power to define that label, and what becomes possible when people claim their own bodies and identities. This lecture is sponsored by the Center for Jewish Studies. 
The event is free and open to the public. 
Accessibility
UNC Asheville is committed to providing universal access to all of our events. If you have any questions about access or would like to request reasonable accommodations that will facilitate your full participation in the film screenings, please contact Stephanie Bullick, Director of Accessibility, at accessibility@unca.edu.

title: Bluegrass and Ice Cream
description:
Hendo Fun Friends
Gathering on the third Sunday evening each month in the Hendersonville Presbyterian Church (HPC) community room, a crowd of up to 200 people enjoy a special blend of bluegrass and gospel music interspersed with humorous anecdotes and inspirational messages — and free ice cream and cookies to boot!

Usually fewer than 20 percent of those attending are members of HPC. The rest of the audience comes from various backgrounds, denominations and ages to hear the combination of original gospel music and old-time Southern gospel songs. A love offering for the band is taken, but giving is strictly voluntary.
HPC is located at the corner of Seventh Avenue and Grove Street. Parking is in the rear of the church and accessible from Grove and King Streets and from Sixth Avenue. For more information about the
church and the Bash, visit hendersonvillepc.org or call the church office, 828-692-3211.

title: Game Night @ Archetype Brewing
description:
Asheville's Bored Game Geeks
tldr: \*\*We are at Archetype Brewing - West!\*\* Bring your favorite game(s) or learn a new one – members are always happy to teach! See you there and have a blast!

🎲🍻 **Welcome to the Game Night Extravaganza!** 🍻🎲

Calling all dice-rollers, card-shufflers, and strategy-curious adventurers! 🌟
Are weeknights feeling a tad mundane? Fear not! We’ve got the antidote: **Board Games, Brews, and Bliss**. 🍺🎮

🔥 **Our Mission:** To ignite laughter, forge alliances, and maybe—just maybe—unleash a few friendly rivalries & battle to the death! 🤪

No PhD in rulebooks required! Whether you’re a Settlers of Catan enthusiast or a Code Names solving ninja, or your first time touching a board game ***we will explain all the rules needed.*** 🏰🎉

Expect:

* **Beer on Tap**: Because rolling dice is better with a pint in hand.
* **Low Brainpower Required**: We’re all about fun, not Fermat’s Last Theorem.
* **Epic Showdowns**: Ticket to Ride routes, Splendor gem heists, and High stakes Camel Up.

Feel free to request any game you’d like to play or bring your own. So gather your guild, stack your resource cards, and let the games begin! May your laughter be loud, your moves be bold, and your victory dances be legendary. 🎭🎲
See you at the table! 🌟🍻

**Feel Free to bring your own games too!**

title: Worlds Edge Tr; a Saunter
description:
Hendo Fun Friends
Located in the western-most backside of Chimney Rock St Pk – above the Edneyville orchards. With vast views of the NC Piedmont. On a clear day, you can see Kings Mtn (80 mi/Charlotte)
Remember - hikes led by ‘the Curmudgeon’ tend to have pleasant surprises.
I will be carrying the ‘Ent-Ward’ that gives us permission to pass thru the forest.
**Difficulty:** “off-trail conditions”. Some very challenging footing along **unfenced** cliff edge; plus 'cliff edge' overlooks. A few steep challenging footing sections. **Middle ¼ mile will be ‘off-trail’ thru brush.**
Bring cutting snips and folding handsaws if you have them.
Up to 8 (only) of you are welcome to join me.
**IF YOU HAVE AN ORANGE VEST; WEAR IT. HUNTING SEASON HAS STARTED. ;-) THEY ARE INEXPENSIVE AT WALMART....**
We are the Sloth Hike Team of WNC: “We will get there when we get there.” We dare to go where the ‘real’ hike groups don’t ***!!***
**https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TQ8H4EK2vt4**
Details:
I am going to **scout, trim and assess** the cliff edge of the World’s Edge Tr near Edneyville;
Length: 2.0 miles round-trip; accum ascent: 300 feet, most on the return on rocky forest rd. Pace: **1.5mph.**
Drive time: 20 min 1-way
Google maps= “Ottanola Gap”
Carpool contributions appreciated. $3.00 suggested
Apprx return time: 2:30pm
**Dogs: ONLY well-trained dogs because of the unfenced cliff edge. And leashes will tangle in the brush.**
WAITLISTED PEOPLE WILL BE ADDED AS DRIVERS SIGN ON.
I currently have 2.5 driver. (limit 9)
Weather Check: Edneyville, NC
Incessant prattlers will be assumed to be having an affair.
**Optional**: after the hike, Dine at Kin’s Chinese Kitchen. 2560 Chimney Rock Rd
We suggest masks and open windows while carpooling. Only you know your own health status so judge accordingly if an event may endanger your health or the health of others.
Please bring an extra pair of shoes to avoid bringing your muddy shoes into the driver's car at the end of the hike.
All hikes are at your own risk. You are responsible for your OWN safety and adequate equipment.
Waiver: There are certain risks inherent in any outdoor activity. Each participant, by signing up to attend this event, agrees to release from liability the leader(s), Hendo Fun Friends, its Partners, Affiliates, and members for any accident, injury, illness, or personal loss which might occur while participating in this activity or while traveling in any vehicle during this trip. **Each participant further agrees to abide by the rules and regulations concerning safety, to follow instructions of the leader(s), and not to become intentionally separated from the group.** The leader(s) also has the right to use any images collected on this trip for recording on website photo collections.

Never played? No problem! Crokinole is easy to learn and endlessly fun. Players take turns flicking wooden discs across a circular board, aiming for the high-scoring center zones. The twist? If your opponent has discs on the board, you must hit one—miss, and your piece is out!

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: Shut Up & Write event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

HOSTS: This is a multi-host event, so most of the time there will be a host present. If we are unlucky and no host can attend, please find each other and self-organize. Pay attention to the event chat and comments to see who is available.

WI-FI: Yes!

PARKING: Street parking in metered spots is free after 6pm. Closest municipal garages ($2/hour) are Wall St. & Coxe Street/Sears Alley.

title: The Leadership Lounge: The Three Pillars
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
You want to do your best work every time. It's important to you, and you care about how you show up and what your team thinks of you.
Being present for ourselves is a significant challenge that often creates a gap. This gap represents the difference between the way we aspire to live and how we actually live. We choose to bridge this gap because it is the right thing to do.

Introducing a great way for new nomads to connect and discover important key takeaways for their lives. As a new Asheville Digital Nomad, where do you go if you don’t know many people?

You will participate in a discussion, yes! YOU, the audience, will be a part of a wonderful panel discussion. Whether you are a veteran or a newbie, come to **The Leadership Lounge**. You will get something out of this event and gain new insights to improve your outlook on how well you are settling into Asheville and Western North Carolina.

**The Leadership Lounge** presents a fabulous evening: **The Three Pillars.** This special occasion will introduce you to new actions to manage burnout and physiological changes, combining practicality with an intuitive desire for more fun.

location: Little Jumbo: 241 Broadway St., Asheville, NC 28801
description:
Every atom in your body was forged in the belly of a dying star. The calcium in your bones, the iron in your blood, the carbon threading through every strand of your DNA — all of it cooked at temperatures beyond human language, scattered across the void, and reassembled over billions of years into something that walks into a bar on a Tuesday night and listens.

Sanders, Boyd, Page & Hall are four collections of stellar debris who have chosen to spend their brief window of consciousness making original music together. Not playing songs. Not running repertoire. Building something in real time from the raw material of attention, instinct, and decades of accumulated craft — compositions that didn't exist before these particular particles arranged themselves around instruments in this part...

title: Blue Ridge Ecosystems – From Ice Age to the Present
description:
Blue Ridge Ecosystems – From Ice Age to the Present
with Dan Lazar 
Wednesday, November 18  |  1 – 3pm 
BRN – Core  |  BREG – Elective 
Register Here!
Blue Ridge ecosystems have changed dramatically since the end of the last ice age 18,000 years ago.  For example, while glaciers still covered northern Ohio and Pennsylvania, the summits of the Great Craggy Mountains, the Black Mountains and the Smokies were treeless and clothed in alpine tundra vegetation, while Mastodons and Giant Ground Sloths roamed the valleys below.  As the climate warmed, the plant and animal communities we see today slowly developed. 
Dan Lazar served for many years as the director of education at the Western North Carolina Nature Center, followed by several years as executive director of the Colburn Earth Science Museum. Dan has a degree in forest biology from the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry and has been an instructor in the Blue Ridge Naturalist program since 2005.

description:
Center for Spiritual Living Asheville
# 🌟 Gratitude Talk with Coach Thomas

### An Uplifting Evening of Gratitude, Reflection & Inspiration

📅 **Wednesday, November 18, 2026**
🕡 **6:30 PM – 7:45 PM**
📍 **Center for Spiritual Living Asheville**
2 Science of Mind Way, Asheville, NC

💛 **Value-Based Love Offering**

Join us for an uplifting and inspiring conversation with **Coach Thomas** as we explore the power of gratitude and how it can gently transform the way we see ourselves, others, and life itself.

Through reflection, insight, and heart-centered awareness, this 1-hour-and-15-minute talk explores how cultivating gratitude can:

✨ Deepen our sense of inner peace
🌱 Strengthen resilience through life's challenges
💛 Transform how we relate to ourselves and others
🌟 Open the door to a more genuine and meaningful life

Gratitude is more than simply saying thank you. It's a way of seeing, experiencing, and embracing life with greater awareness and appreciation.

title: AYPROS Night at UNC Asheville Men's Basketball
description:
Asheville Young Professionals (AYPROS)
**Bulldogs basketball. An entire section reserved for AYPROS. Our first beer courtesy of Bear's Smokehouse BBQ. Commemorative cups. A special shoutout during the game. And a group photo ON THE COURT afterward. All with tickets for just $5!**
We're teaming up with UNC Asheville Athletics for a special AYPROS Night at Kimmel Arena on **Wednesday, November 18**, as the Bulldogs take on the Tennessee Tech Golden Eagles!
Our friends at UNC Asheville are rolling out the welcome mat for Asheville's young professionals. We've got our own reserved seating in Section 6 so we can cheer on the Bulldogs together, and UNC Asheville is planning a special **AYPROS announcement over the arena's PA system during the game.** Even better? After the final buzzer, we'll have the opportunity to head down onto the basketball court for an official AYPROS group photo!
How often do you get to walk onto the court at Kimmel Arena? We're hoping to fill Section 6 with as many AYPROS members as possible, so grab your friends, coworkers, significant others, or anyone who enjoys a great night of college basketball. Whether you're a die-hard Bulldogs fan or haven't been to a game in years, this is a pretty great excuse to get out, meet some new people, and show some love for our hometown team.

### And There's More! Your First Beer Is on Bear's!

Our friends at **Bear's Smokehouse BBQ** are making AYPROS Night even better by purchasing the **first beer for our AYPROS attendees (21+)!**
A huge thank you to **Cheryl Antoncic-Suess and the entire Bear's Smokehouse BBQ team** for generously stepping up to treat our crew. Bear's operates concessions at Kimmel Arena, and we're grateful they're helping us make this a special night for Asheville's young professionals.
AYPROS attendees 21 and older will receive a drink voucher redeemable at Bear's concession stands. Just bring your ID!
And that's not all. There will also be **special commemorative cups given out that evening**.
Between the game, our reserved section, a beer courtesy of Bear's, the commemorative cups, our in-game recognition, and the opportunity to get everyone together on the court afterward, this is shaping up to be a pretty special evening!

### The First 20 AYPROS Attendees Get In FREE!

That's right! **AYPROS is purchasing tickets for the first 20 AYPROS attendees who arrive at the game.** We're covering the cost of admission for our early arrivals as one more reason to come out and join us.
And if you're not among the first 20? **Tickets are only $5 (normally $25) with our exclusive AYPROS discount code.** That's an 80% discount on Division I college basketball, with a few AYPROS-only perks thrown in for good measure.
Want to make sure you've got a seat? You can purchase your $5 ticket in advance using the instructions below.

### Game Day Details

* **Date:** Wednesday, November 18, 2026
* **Time:** 6:30 PM (doors open at 5:30 PM)
* **Matchup:** UNC Asheville Bulldogs vs. Tennessee Tech Golden Eagles
* **Location:** Kimmel Arena, Sherrill Center at UNC Asheville, 227 Campus Drive, Asheville, NC 28804
* **AYPROS Seating:** Section 6
* **Tickets:** Just $5 with promo code **AYPROS**
* **First Beer:** Courtesy of Bear's Smokehouse BBQ for AYPROS attendees ages 21+
* **Special Extras:** Commemorative cup giveaway, in-game AYPROS recognition, and an official postgame group photo on the court
* **What to Wear:** Your best BULLDOGS BLUE! We want to see a sea of blue in our section and in our group photo. (Not sure what Bulldog Blue is? [Check out the university's style guide here](https://www.unca.edu/communication/branding/graphic-standards/)!)

### How to Get Your $5 Tickets

1. Click **[Purchase Your AYPROS Tickets Here](https://university-of-north-carolina-asheville-ilh9.vivenushop.com/event/6a79dfcabe06b62435059128/6ab535875a3b4d739107f1a1)**.
2. Select "Buy Tickets" and enter promo code **AYPROS** when prompted.
3. Choose your seats in Section 6 and complete your purchase.

We've reserved Section 6 specifically for AYPROS, and we'd love nothing more than to fill it! Tickets are available directly through UNC Asheville Athletics, so be sure to purchase yours and encourage your friends to do the same.

### Parking & Arrival Information

Parking for UNC Asheville basketball games is included in your game ticket, so there is no additional parking charge.
**Important:** UNC Asheville requires all campus visitors to register their vehicles, even when parking is included with admission.

* **Where to Park:** Public campus lots P8, P10, P11, P12, P14, P15, and P16 are within walking distance of Kimmel Arena.
* **Reserved Parking:** The P9 parking deck adjacent to the arena is reserved for qualifying Bulldog Club members, with accessible parking available for properly permitted vehicles.
* **Parking Registration:** [Register your vehicle here](https://unca.aimsparking.com/) before arriving. There is no additional charge for basketball game attendees.
* **Arena Entry:** Doors open at 5:30 PM, one hour before tip-off.
* **Campus Map:** [View UNC Asheville's parking information and campus map](https://uncabulldogs.com/sports/2025/8/21/parking-on-campus/).

We recommend arriving a little early to find parking, get settled in Section 6, and take advantage of everything planned for the evening.

### Let's Fill Section 6!

A huge thank you to **Kassi Butcher and the UNC Asheville Athletics team** for helping put this evening together, and to **Cheryl Antoncic Suess and Bear's Smokehouse BBQ** for treating our attendees to their first beer!
**Now let's show UNC Asheville what the AYPROS community can do!** We're hoping to pack Section 6, make some noise for our hometown Bulldogs, and get as many of us as possible into that postgame photo. But we need you there to make it happen.
Grab your $5 ticket, send this invitation to a few friends, and come dressed in your best Bulldogs blue. The more of us who show up, the better this night will be.

Use promo code **AYPROS**, and let's fill those stands!

Self-Care and Community of Practice Led by Black Facilitators, for the Black Community.

About this Event
"Caring for myself is not self - indulgence; it is self-preservation, and that is an act of political warfare." Audre Lorde

This is an invitation specifically for persons who identify as Black or African American and are overwhelmed with the injustice of the world and are ready to create space in their lives for self-care as we fight for justice for all! (We offer a parallel session for Allies to connect, learn and find support in their work to dismantle racism at allies.eventbrite.com)

We believe Black people deserve a space to relax, reassess, and realign ourselves.

We are a collective of Black stress-management & wellness instructors inspired by human values.

We are here to facilitate your journey of trauma-relief and stress-management.

Imagine how much more energy you will have and how much more powerful you will be when you cut your stress levels in half!

And it can be done in just a few minutes using nothing but your own breath...

Over the last 10 years, we've taught over 100,000 people to do just that.
The key is that your breath is directly linked to your emotions.

This 1-Hour Restorative Session Includes:
-Open, safe space for sharing and self-care for Black people
-Facilitated discussion
-Breath work and meditation

Led by Black facilitators, certified in stress and trauma relief.
Unleash the Hidden Healing Power of the Breath

title: Gratitude: Connecting with the Heart Through Creative Expression
description:
Gratitude: Connecting with the Heart Through Creative Expression
with Catherine Willows 
Thursday, November 19  |  10 am – 1 pm 
Register Here!
In the depths of autumn, Thanksgiving invites a pause—to step outside the momentum of everyday life, connect with your heart, and open to the energy of gratitude. Gathering together in the Arboretum gardens, we’ll attune to the natural world of the season and the quiet wisdom within. Gratitude is more than something you think about or name. It is an energy, a quality of presence, a frequency. When you pause long enough to connect with it, something shifts—awakening a greater receptivity to the richness of what is here, to what has touched and nourished you, and to what is quietly ready to be revealed. 
Through intuitive painting, guided reflection, and expressive art-making, we’ll explore gratitude through color, imagery, symbols, and words. Noticing what catches your attention and allowing the creative process to lead, space opens for what is within to become visible, felt, or known in its own way. 
No artistic experience is needed, only curiosity, a willingness to listen inwardly, and an openness to discover what reveals itself. All art materials will be provided. 
Catherine Willows is a Registered Nurse, Certified Functional Medicine Health Coach, and Transformational Creativity Coach, and founder of Willows Coaching and Consulting. While holding sacred space, she guides adults in awakening their inner creativity — moving beyond the demands of daily life into greater flow, self-discovery, and joy through intuitive art-making processes. Catherine believes creativity and our connection to the natural world are deeply interwoven — both vital pillars of wellbeing, supporting nervous system regulation and inner equanimity, and together essential for living a meaningful, embodied life aligned with purpose and authentic expression.

* All parts of you are welcome.
* Our team are experienced in creating safe online spaces for young LGBTQ+ people to meet, connect, share and support each other. Oh, and we really like music - so we'll be playing some of that too!
* Input always welcome and you are free to participate in the chat in any way you feel safe to do so. Feel like turning camera off - that's fine, feeling like you want to stay quiet - fine as well, want to share a poem, painting or magic trick - you are very welcome!
* We will also be available to answer questions about the other forms of mental health support we have available here at Rainbow Mind.
*

**All members of the LGBTQ+ community are invited, whether you identify with an individual letter of the acronym, more than one or are unsure of how you identify.**
Thank you and we look forward to seeing you,
The Rainbow Mind Young People Project Team
*Please note: this workshop is intended to be for LGBTQ+ young people aged between 17-24. Participants that do not fit this demographic will respectfully be asked to re-book on to a more appropriate event. bit.ly/TheGatherings*

title: AYPROS x Bounty & Soul: Market Support Volunteer Day
description:
Asheville Young Professionals (AYPROS)
**Help us make a difference in our community, one market day at a time!**

Join AYPROS for an afternoon of volunteering with Bounty & Soul in Black Mountain!

We'll be helping out at Bounty & Soul's Bi-Lo Market, where volunteers play an important role in keeping things organized, welcoming, and running smoothly for community members.

From distributing available food and other items to helping participants carry things to their vehicles, there are plenty of ways to lend a hand.

No special experience needed! Just bring a willingness to help, a friendly attitude, and some comfortable shoes.

## Event Details

* **Date:** Thursday, November 19, 2026
* **Time:** 3:00–5:30 PM
* **Location:** Bounty & Soul Bi-Lo Market, 205 NC-9, Black Mountain, NC
* **Registration:** Free \| Limited to 12 volunteers

## What We'll Be Doing

Our group will help Bounty & Soul staff with a variety of market support tasks, including:

* Distributing available items to market participants
* Helping participants understand quantities and keeping items organized
* Making sure the market stays welcoming and runs smoothly
* Assisting participants with carrying items to their vehicles when needed
* Helping with other tasks depending on the market's needs

It's a hands-on opportunity to support a local nonprofit while spending an afternoon giving back alongside fellow young professionals.

## What to Know Before You Go

* **Arrival:** Please arrive on time and check in with Bounty & Soul staff at the trucks when you arrive.
* **Waivers:** All volunteers must complete Bounty & Soul's liability waiver before participating. You can [\[download the volunteer waiver here\]](https://aypros.wildapricot.org/resources/Bounty%20and%20Soul%20Liability%20Waiver%20and%20Photo%20Release.pdf) and bring the completed form with you, or fill one out on-site.
* **What to wear:** Closed-toe shoes and shirts with sleeves are required. Appropriate shorts or jeans are fine.
* **Weather:** This is an outdoor market, so dress for the conditions. The event may take place in sunshine, cooler temperatures, or light rain.
* **Physical activity:** Expect standing and walking throughout the shift, with some light to moderate lifting. Volunteers can decline tasks they aren't physically comfortable performing.
* **Age requirements:** Volunteers must be at least 16 to participate independently. Ages 14–15 may volunteer with an adult.

## Why It Matters

Bounty & Soul relies on volunteers to help create a welcoming, organized market experience for the people it serves.

By helping with the day-to-day operations, we're supporting the organization's work and making it easier for community members to access available food and other resources.

Whether you're a regular AYPROS volunteer or joining us for the first time, we'd love to have you!

**Only 12 volunteer spots are available, so please register in advance to join us!**

Come spend an afternoon doing something good for our neighbors and connecting with fellow young professionals along the way.

### Need Help Finding Us?

If you have trouble locating the group or are running a few minutes behind, call or text AYPROS Crew Leader **Danielle Klein** at **239-287-8952**.

## About AYPROS Leadership & Service

At AYPROS, leadership is not only about titles. It is about stepping forward, showing up, and doing work that matters.
Our Leadership & Service events give young professionals the opportunity to work alongside local organizations addressing real needs across Asheville and Western North Carolina. This cleanup is a chance to serve the community, care for the French Broad River, and get to know others who want to make Asheville stronger.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Beginning Botany
description:
Beginning Botany
with Alexandra Holland 
Friday, November 20  |  1 – 4pm 
BRN and BREG Core 
Register Here!
It’s a tough life for a plant: make dinner, create and nurture offspring, fight off predators, deal with the neighbors. In Beginning Botany we’ll explore how plants handle these daily challenges using and modifying only leaves, stems, and roots. We’ll cover the basics of plant structure and function. 
Alexandra Holland has a passion for getting people excited about the natural world through classes, hikes, and photography.  She graduated from Duke University and earned her master’s degree in botany from the University of Texas at Austin.  While in Texas, Alexandra managed the UTEX Culture Collection of Algae at UT Austin and volunteered with education programs at the Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center.  Upon moving to Asheville, she began volunteering with the NC Arboretum’s youth education programs.  In 2008 she was in the first class of students to be certified as Blue Ridge Naturalists.   Alexandra teaches botany classes at the NC Arboretum and leads nature hikes in Western NC for groups of all ages.

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: Without Shade, Without Rest Film Screening and Discussion
location: Kittredge Arts Center, Kittredge Theater
description:
Join us November 20, at 6pm in Kittredge Theater for a screening of the film Without Shade, Without Rest. There will be light refreshments provided and a discussion of farm and food worker rights following the film. This screening is made possible by the Educating Character Initiative. 

 

WeCount! is a non-profit, human rights organization that represents immigrant workers and families in South Florida, including plant nursery workers. WeCount!’s advocacy on extreme heat is the subject of the new documentary, Without Shade, Without Rest by Six Eye Films and Working Films. This documentary tells the story of two organizations, WeCount! and the Coalition of Immokalee Workers, and our efforts to win heat protections for Florida’s outdoor workers. In the face of intense industry lobbying and aggressive state preemption, the fight in Florida continues. Their work has helped put extreme heat in the national conversation and inspired advocacy for workplace heat standards across the country. 

 

While “Without Shade, Without Rest” is primarily focused on Florida, we believe this film can be a helpful tool for workers, advocates, organizations, and community members across the country and world, who are similarly grappling with the growing and existential threat of climate change and extreme heat. We hope the film helps shine a light on an urgent labor and human rights issue and contributes to meaningful dialogue and connections across our movements. In Asheville, a new campaign Planting Justice (Sembra Justicia) is being launched by WeCount! and local partners in support of workers in the house plant industry who work locally with little labor protections. The food we eat and the plants we enjoy are nothing without the workers who plant and nurture them.

title: See the Sights of Cherokee on a 10 KM/6.2 mile Walk
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
We'll gather at the Welcome Center across from the fairgrounds. Our route takes us past the Museum of the Cherokee People and the Qualla Arts and Crafts facility. We then walk the road up to the *Unto These Hills* Amphitheatre. From there we pass the Oconaluftee Indian Village and walk through the Botanical Gardens. Coming back down the back way, we loop around ending up at the Oconaluftee Islands Park with its "bamboo forest." From there we return to the start point.

Hiking boots are not needed, though some will want walking poles. (I plan to take both of mine.) Do bring plenty of water and a protein snack. Dress for the weather. I'm not sure whether dogs are allowed in the Botanical Gardens, but it is a short loop and if necessary, you can walk around the parking lot for the few minutes it will take us to make that loop. While much of this walk is on pavement, trail strollers would be needed for the walk, with a few workarounds.

Drive into Cherokee on US-441. When you pass the Cherokee movie theater, the highway will turn left. Look for the fairgrounds on your left and the Welcome Center on your right. We will gather in the parking lot. There are restrooms in the Welcome Center.

title: Mammals of the Southern Appalachians
description:
Mammals of the Southern Appalachians
with Carlton Burke 
Saturday, November 21  |  12 – 4pm 
BRN – Core  |  BREG – Elective 
Register Here!
The rugged mountains of Appalachia host a tremendous variety of mammal species ranging from tiny shrews weighing only a few ounces at most to huge mammals such as the black bear which can weigh in at several hundred pounds. Also large mammals such as the cougar, bison, and elk also once commonly roamed these mountains. In this class we will discuss present and past mammals of the region, their distribution, natural life cycles, and also controversies and cultural connections they have with the ever increasing human population of the area.  Class participants will also have a chance to meet a few live, native mammal species of the mountain region as well. 
Carlton Burke is a naturalist and educator who operates Carolina Mountain Naturalists, an educational service which offers wildlife and nature educational programs throughout western North Carolina. He also was on the staff of the western North Carolina Nature Center in Asheville for over 25 years as the Curator of Exhibits. Carlton co-hosts a weekly radio program NATURE NEWS and is also a NC state and federally licensed wildlife rehabilitator.

title: NOBODY'S DARLING STRING BAND
description:
Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.



Band Members include Dona Cavanagh, fiddle; Zena Rubin, banjo-uke; Maxine Herring, rhythm guitar; Hilary Dirlam, melody guitar; and Celia Millington-Wyckoff, bass.



The five women comprising Nobody’s Darling each have a long history of playing old-time music. Individually they have played in many other bands through the years, including The Carolina Oldtimers, The Pegtwisters, The Zuma House Band, Too Hot To Cook, The Luke Smathers Mountain Swing Band, Honey Holler, and The Carolina Chick Peas.



Stop in to enjoy the music and an afternoon libation or two, perhaps with an early supper or light bite . . . and don't forget your dancing shoes!

title: Jackson Grimm's Old Time Machine
description:
Jackson Grimm marries folk pop melodies with the lonesome sound of traditional Appalachian music. 



His Appalachian-infused Americana songs run the gamut from a traditional country waltz homage ("If Not For You") to an unrequited love song driven by a Beatles-esque melody ("I'd Hold You, But I Don't Wanna Hold You)" to a drunken Old Crow Medicine Show-style partygrass number ("Last Train Home").



Grimm studied Traditonal Music at Warren Wilson College under the tutelage of renowned players like Wayne Erbsen and Kevin Kehrberg. He also studied guitar, banjo, mandolin & singing with the Western North Carolina music master, Josh Goforth.



He also plays extensively as a sideman for his father, singer-songwriter Tim Grimm, touring all over the US and to Europe. Jackson has appeared on, written songs on, and co-produced the last two Tim Grimm albums. He's has also shared the stage and played with singer-songwriters Ben Bedford, Krista Detor, Jennie DeVoe & Old Sap.



Still a hometown boy, Grimm can be found playing solo or around Western North Carolina with Holler Choir, One Stringband, or his Old Time Machine.



Music 8:30-11:30pm, $10 cover at the door.

title: Exhibition on Screen | The Danish Collector: Delacroix to Gauguin
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
For many years no-one was interested in the art of the Impressionists. Artists like Monet, Degas and Renoir were vilified, attacked, and left penniless as a result. Then, something remarkable happened. A new breed of collectors emerged and, before long, they were battling to acquire any work by these new, radical artists that they could find. Amongst them was the visionary Danish businessman Wilhelm Hansen. It was an extraordinary moment in art history; full of drama, intrigue and subterfuge. Some collectors we may recognize and some we may not, but Hansen amassed a remarkable collection housed at his summer home, Ordrupgaard, on the outskirts of Copenhagen. Exhibition on Screen tells his fascinating story and, with exclusive access to a sell- out exhibition at London’s Royal Academy, brings the extraordinary collection to the big-screen in glorious high-definition. From Hansen’s beautiful house and gardens at Ordrupgaard to the streets of bohemian Paris, this film takes you on a journey to discover some of the best examples of 19th-century French art ever collected. 
Purchase Tickets 
Directed by David Bickerstaff

title: Mountains-to-Sea Trail Highway 25 toward Bent Creek
description:
Asheville Mountains-to-Sea Trail Hiking Club 2.0
This is a fairly easy hike, and we go at a high average to low advanced speed, which is roughly about 3.0 to 3.2 mph. There are no super long hills. It's pretty undulating all the way.

Well behaved dogs on leashes are welcome to attend.

When you arrive, park at the gravel lot across from the trail head. You'll see some people gathering by their cars. I've recently corrected the PIN setting on the map, so it should be correct. Here are some directions to use too: When going south on Hendersonville Road, go past Carolina Day School and turn right at the Blue Ridge Parkway exit. When you get to the parkway turn RIGHT. You will see parking on the left and right side of the road. Park there.

Mountains-to-Sea-Trail hikes are designed for fitness and community among people who are already reasonably fit. It's not an endurance hike by any means, but it is designed so we can get our hearts beating a bit while still being able to have a conversation and meet new people.
When you arrive, we'll circle up and introduce ourselves briefly. There will be a person who is a sweep. This person is the person who walks last and makes sure no one gets lost.

We leave the parking spot at 9:10. If someone needs a nature break, we wait fo you, but it's not a hike where we stop and take photos or frequent breaks. We basically keep hiking until the 1/2 way mark, then turn around after a short (approximately 5 minute) break. Then we keep that same pace on the way back. If we get on a trail right at 9:10, we are normally finished around 10:50.

These are out and back hikes, meaning that we hike in and turn around half way to return back.

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: Shut Up & Write event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

HOSTS: This is a multi-host event, so most of the time there will be a host present. If we are unlucky and no host can attend, please find each other and self-organize. Pay attention to the event chat and comments to see who is available.

WI-FI: Yes!

PARKING: Street parking in metered spots is free after 6pm. Closest municipal garages ($2/hour) are Wall St. & Coxe Street/Sears Alley.

title: Manifesting Self
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**Location Change:**
**Disclaimer: In all efforts to keep this Meetup a safe space, we all agree to keep anything said within the group private and confidential.**

Do you want to take your remote working game to the next level? Do you find yourself saying wtf is Manifesting Self??

Well, you’re not alone. Remote working is glamorous, and also presents itself with challenges not seen in the traditional office environment.

Manifesting Self may sound a little out there. Trust me. It’s not. Whether we’ve been in the remote space for years, since the pandemic, or just recently, I’m certain it has changed each of us in ways we never thought possible. Let’s explore that together. We are so excited to see you, again or for the first time!

Routes-
1 miler:
RIGHT out of OLR parking lot
Continue around roundabout at Clingman, and head toward the river on Lyman St.

Right on the Greenway to the Craven St Park put in (the dock)
Turn around and go back the same way to OLR

3 miler:

Continue onto Craven St. Bridge
LEFT onto Greenway after bridge
Follow Greenway all the way until it ends at Haywood Rd.

Cross the Roundabout at Roberts St. and continue onto Clingman
Continue on Clingman
LEFT onto Owens Bell Lane
LEFT onto Hilliard at the top of the hill
LEFT onto W Haywood, follow all the way down to Roberts
LEFT onto Roberts
Follow Roberts back to OLR
Pass OLR to Bartlett, turn around and come back to OLR

Cross back over the bridge on Amboy and run the Greenway back to the roundabout
Follow Lyman back to OLR

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

description:

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: Shut Up & Write - South Asheville
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
Coworking for writers in your area!
Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.

Please arrive a few minutes early to say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.

Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!

A note about the format
We don’t host critiques or readings. These events are a safe space for writers of all skill levels and genres to work on their craft, so no one will read or critique your writing.

For our full event schedule, visit https://shutupwrite.com

Other Important Details:

Venue Guidelines: Please thank our hosts by purchasing something.

title: BECOMING YOUR MOST GENUINE SELF: A Journey Back to Who You Really Are
description:
Center for Spiritual Living Asheville
BECOMING YOUR MOST GENUINE SELF: A Journey Back to Who You Really Are
✨ A Workshop with Thomas J. Brady, founder of Energy Culture LLC

Who are you when you remove the expectations of others, the labels you've accepted, and the limitations you've placed upon yourself?

What if becoming your most genuine self isn't about changing who you are, but discovering who you've always been?

Join Thomas J. Brady for an inspiring journey of self-discovery, personal growth, and authentic connection.

Through meaningful conversation, guided reflection, and practical exercises, we'll explore the beliefs, experiences, and patterns that influence how we see ourselves and the world around us.

Together, we'll explore:
🌿 Self-Discovery: Recognizing the beliefs and patterns that may be holding you back.
💛 Healing & Release: Learning to let go of what no longer serves your growth.
✨ Authenticity & Purpose: Reconnecting with your values, your inner wisdom, and the person you truly wish to become.
🤝 Genuine Connection: Creating meaningful connections through openness, understanding, and acceptance.

Thomas is the creator of Energy Culture LLC and author of the Star children's book series, stories designed to inspire imagination, kindness, courage, and the belief that every individual carries something extraordinary within them.

At the heart of this workshop is a simple belief:

When we begin to change the way we see ourselves, we begin to change the world we experience.
You don't need to have all the answers. You don't need to be anyone other than yourself.

Come as you are. Discover what is possible.

💛 All are welcome. No judgment. Just love.

Be the you that the world needs.

description:

Dress for the weather. Consider a hat and sunscreen. Some people may want walking poles, especially for the walk up to Lambuth Inn; tennis shoes should be fine. It is particularly important that walkers bring a protein snack and **plenty of** **water**. Restrooms are available at the Welcome Center, at Lambuth Inn, and along the route. Dogs on leash are welcome. Strollers are ok.
