title: Birding for Beginners
description:
Birding for Beginners
with Shane Myers 
Tuesday, December 1  |  9 – 10:30am 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
Join us on this birding walk around the NC Arboretum gardens and trails in search of our most colorful residents. We will go over best practices for using binoculars, recommendations for purchasing your own binoculars, and popular field guides to use. Bring your own binoculars but if you do not have a pair we have some loaner binoculars available to use during the programs. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Shane Myers’ interest in nature began as a child with a love of dinosaurs. This quickly grew to include fossils, insects, and reptiles, and learning from the notes his grandparents kept of the birds that came to their feeders in Toledo, Ohio.  He has a Bachelors of Science in Wildlife Biology and did most of his undergraduate work on dragonflies and damselflies. He’s assisted in outreach and education for plant conservation groups, Odonata Groups, and various bird groups. Shane currently works for the Adult Education department at the NC Arboretum.

title: AVL Digital Nomads - Book Club
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**December 2026 Selection - *When Breach Becomes Air* by Paul Kalanithi**
[Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/When-Breath-Becomes-Paul-Kalanithi/dp/081298840X/) - [GoodReads](https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/25899336-when-breath-becomes-)

*At the age of thirty-six, on the verge of completing a decade’s worth of training as a neurosurgeon, Paul Kalanithi was diagnosed with stage IV lung cancer. One day he was a doctor treating the dying, and the next he was a patient struggling to live. And just like that, the future he and his wife had imagined evaporated. When Breath Becomes Air chronicles Kalanithi’s transformation from a naïve medical student “possessed,” as he wrote, “by the question of what, given that all organisms die, makes a virtuous and meaningful life” into a neurosurgeon at Stanford working in the brain, the most critical place for human identity, and finally into a patient and new father confronting his own mortality.*

*What makes life worth living in the face of death? What do you do when the future, no longer a ladder toward your goals in life, flattens out into a perpetual present? What does it mean to have a child, to nurture a new life as another fades away? These are some of the questions Kalanithi wrestles with in this profoundly moving, exquisitely observed memoir.*

*Paul Kalanithi died in March 2015, while working on this book, yet his words live on as a guide and a gift to us all. “I began to realize that coming face to face with my own mortality, in a sense, had changed nothing and everything,” he wrote. “Seven words from Samuel Beckett began to repeat in my head: ‘I can’t go on. I’ll go on.’” When Breath Becomes Air is an unforgettable, life-affirming reflection on the challenge of facing death and on the relationship between doctor and patient, from a brilliant writer who became both.*

\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-

**Welcome to our monthly Book Club!** We’re a small, friendly group that gets together for fun, thoughtful conversations about a different book each month.

Finished the whole book? Great. Only made it through a few chapters? Still come. Didn’t read it at all but the discussion sounds interesting? Honestly, you’re welcome too.
We meet on the **first Tuesday of every month**.

One of the best things about this group is that we keep it relatively small and guide the conversation, so it doesn’t turn into three people talking while everyone else quietly questions their life choices. Everyone has a chance to jump in, share their thoughts, and explore the book’s characters, themes, writing, and bigger ideas.

You definitely don’t need to be a literary expert. Whether you read constantly or you’re trying to get back into it, this is a relaxed place to discover new books, hear different perspectives, and meet some great people along the way.

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

* Whatever you need to be able to write!

title: The Next Five: Build ADN’s 2027 Together
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
Ever wondered how AVL Digital Nomads actually works, who makes it happen, and where it’s headed next? Come find out, and help decide.

ADN has almost 6,000 members and zero employees. Every social, lunch, book club, and workshop on our calendar exists because a nomad decided it should. This evening is a look behind the curtain: where we’ve been, where we’re going, and the many ways to be part of it. It’s built as much for people who joined this year as for longtime regulars.

We’re gathering where ADN began in 2021: Wedge Brewing at Foundation, in the new community room they built after Helene. It felt like the right place to start the next chapter.

**What happens**

* **Where ADN is headed:** A short, honest look at the mission and what’s next.
* **“My First Event” stories:** Longtime organizers share how they got started, mishaps included.
* **The Idea Wall:** Ideas from RSVPs go up on the wall. Add yours and vote with dot stickers. Have an idea already? Share it when you RSVP. It’s optional
* **The No-Shark Tank:** Anyone can pitch an event idea in 60 seconds. Nobody gets eaten, and listening counts.
* **Huddles:** Join the conversation that interests you. Some people leave with a plan, and everyone leaves knowing more nomads than they came with.

Come curious. No idea, commitment, or experience required.

title: Handmade Holiday: Wild Ornaments
description:
Handmade Holiday: Wild Ornaments
with Carleigh Fairchild 
Wednesday, December 2  |  10 am – 1 pm 
Register Here!
Using cattail leaves and colored ribbons we will make several different styles of ornaments: animal shapes and star shapes. 
Previous basket making or weaving experience is not necessary but you will use fine motor skills to make these ornaments. You will have the opportunity to make many during our time together, to decorate your tree or to give as gifts. All materials are provided in this class. 
Carleigh Fairchild has a deep love for the Earth. She gardens, keeps bees, wild harvests, processes animals, tans hides, weaves baskets, and finds joy in time spent around the fire. As the founder of Human Nature Connection LLC, she is dedicated to helping others rediscover respectful and collaborative relationships with the more then human world. Carleigh’s journey—including 86 days on the survival show ALONE in Patagonia—deepened her understanding of belonging and connection. With over 25 years of experience, she teaches both online and in-person classes in Western North Carolina, weaving together earth skills, community, and healing. Carleigh is also a NIASZIIH bodywork healer and instructor at Wilderness Fusion, integrating body, earth, and spirit in her practice.

title: The Polyvagal Sangha
description:
Inner Peace Collective
**The Polyvagal Sangha**
*A community of seekers exploring nervous system regulation through the lens of ancient wisdom and modern science.*

A new tribe is forming. We're inviting 30 like-minded and like-hearted folks into an ongoing inquiry — learning to cultivate a greater felt sense of calm, ease, safety, and resilience in our bodies, our relationships, and the world around us. The goal isn't just personal regulation, but a ripple effect of co-regulation: a shift in how we show up for others and move through our own lives.

This is the first class in a 3-class series. The whole is greater than the sum of its parts, yet a single dive will yield beneficial results towards salutogenesis.

**Teachers:** Omri Sitton, D.C. and Wills Reed, LCMHCA

**Cost:** $10–$15 suggested donation to local nonprofit *Source Of Wellness*.
\*No one is turned away for lack of funds — all donations are appreciated.

**How to Reserve Your Spot** (please do both — priority goes to folks who complete both steps):

1. **Text Omri at 828-298-0011** with your name and whether you'd like to pay via Venmo or at the door
2. **RSVP on Meetup** using the button on this page

*A note on the two-step process: based on past events, people who only RSVP on Meetup often don't show up. Texting Omri directly helps us plan for who's actually coming — so please do both.*

**A Bit More Detail:**
Polyvagal Theory (PVT) — conceptualized by Stephen Porges — reveals how our body and brain collaborate to respond to everyday stress and deeply held trauma. It highlights the role of the autonomic nervous system, especially the vagus nerve, in shaping our physical and mental health. Paired with mindfulness practices drawn from ancient traditions, PVT offers us both the science and the felt experience of coming back to our center.

By building community together, we naturally stimulate the social engagement system — the nervous system's highest branch — fostering connection, safety, and ease in body, mind, and life. This is the essence of The Polyvagal Sangha.

**Participants will learn:**

* Polyvagal Theory's three defining principles
* Somatic activities specific to each branch of the autonomic nervous system
* Awareness practices to soften emotional triggers and past traumas
* The body's innate biological responses, and the role of mindfulness in being present to "what is"
* How connecting with others committed to personal growth naturally lifts and supports us all

Join Omri and Wills for a series of illustrated, experiential presentations that will inspire your spirit, engage your mind, and challenge your creativity — as you uncover the enormous potential of applying this work in your daily life.

*Feel Well. Heal Well. Live Well.*

**About the teachers:**

**About Omri**
Omri Sitton, D.C., Cert. ZB has 25 years of experience in multiple fields of the healing arts. His passion in helping others has a strong emphasis on self-care.

He naturally weaves the connection between mindfulness practice, cellular consciousness, and polyvagal theory into his experiential classes.

Dr. Omri practices Tonal Chiropractic, Zero Balancing, and Polyvagal Touch in Asheville, offering what he refers to as ChiroSomatics.
Learn more at [omsourcewellness.com](https://www.omsourcewellness.com/)

**About Wills**
Wills Reed, LCMHCA, is an Asheville-based psychotherapist with a particular interest in how our earliest relationships, life experiences, and nervous systems shape the way we experience ourselves and others.

His work draws from attachment-focused therapy, EMDR, somatic approaches, and a longtime personal practice of meditation and contemplative traditions. He enjoys helping people translate these ideas into practical experiences of greater safety, connection, and freedom in everyday life.

title: Thursday Run
description:
Asheville Runners
Come run 1, 3, or 6 miles and stay for a beer and soccer tennis after at Olde London Road.

Routes-
1 miler:
RIGHT out of OLR parking lot
Continue around roundabout at Clingman, and head toward the river on Lyman St.
RIGHT on River Arts Place
Cross Riverside onto the Greenway
Right on the Greenway to the Craven St Park put in (the dock)
Turn around and go back the same way to OLR

3 miler:
Start the same as 1 miler
Continue onto Craven St. Bridge
LEFT onto Greenway after bridge
Follow Greenway all the way until it ends at Haywood Rd.
RIGHT onto Haywood Rd, go across the bridge
Cross the Roundabout at Roberts St. and continue onto Clingman
Continue on Clingman
LEFT onto Owens Bell Lane
LEFT onto Hilliard at the top of the hill
LEFT onto W Haywood, follow all the way down to Roberts
LEFT onto Roberts
Follow Roberts back to OLR
Pass OLR to Bartlett, turn around and come back to OLR

6 miler:
After the W Haywood downhill to Roberts
LEFT onto Roberts St. take to Lyman and head back to the Greenway
LEFT onto the Greenway, take all the way to Amboy
RIGHT on Amboy to cross the bridge
RIGHT into French Broad River Park, run the loop at the park
Cross back over the bridge on Amboy and run the Greenway back to the roundabout
Follow Lyman back to OLR

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: Agenda Keeper Launch Party!
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**AVL Tech Connect: Product Launch Party!**
Friday, December 4 · 6:30 to 10 PM
The Mule at Devil’s Foot, Asheville, NC
Free and open to the public

After countless hours of design and development, extended user interviews and surveys, dedicated UX whiteboard sessions, and product meetings (so many meetings), [Agenda Keeper](https://agendakeeper.com) is officially launching to the public, and we want to celebrate with the community that helped shape it.

Join us at The Mule at Devil’s Foot for a night with a DJ, a live band, and a food truck. This one is about taking a moment to enjoy what we built and to cheer on the local team behind it.

**What to expect**

* Music from a DJ and a live band
* Food truck eats
* A quick, casual hello about what Agenda Keeper is and why we built it
* Time to meet the team at Aktiga and connect with Asheville’s tech community

Agenda Keeper is a meeting agenda tool built by the friendly folks at [Aktiga](https://aktiga.com) that helps teams plan and manage recurring meetings, collaborate on notes, capture key decisions, and follow through on action items. It’s free to start. No pitch deck, no hard sell. Come say hi, grab a beverage (lots of great NA options!), and celebrate with us.

Everyone is welcome. Tech folks, nomads, founders, and friends.
No Agenda? No Thanks. 🙌

title: Scenic AVL - Camino de Brevard w/ WNC Pilgrims
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
**Overview:** This hike is offered as a monthly training hike with the WNC Asheville Chapter of the association of American Pilgrims on the Camino. The route has been announced on the WNC Camino Group [Facebook Group Page](https://www.facebook.com/groups/AVLCamino/announcements).

**Distance:** 4, 8, or 11 miles
**Elevation Gain:** 600 ft in small chunks
**Surface:** Road
**Pace: 3.2 mph**
**Dogs:** Well-behaved dogs on leash.
**Gear:** Water, sunscreen, snacks, cash / payment method for the farmer's market.

**Origin of Route:** This route was created by Kacey R for the WNC Chapter of the American Society of Pilgrims on the Camino.

**All Trails Route Map:** [Brevard Camino Route](https://www.alltrails.com/explore/custom-routes/brevard-camino-k-ratterjee-568e974?u=i&sh=ifwm3x)
The route has 3 sections, each about 4 miles long. Choose the distance that works for you!

**Start:** Transylvania County Public Library
212 S Gaston St, Brevard, NC 28712
Note: The library will be closed at the start, so no bathrooms will be available.

**Want to sleep in?** Meet us at the farmer's market next to St. Phillips Church at around 10:30. [256 E Main St, Brevard, NC 28712](https://maps.app.goo.gl/TeVDqeSEEQD9ieTz7)

**Coffee Break:** There will be a stop at the Farmer's Market at about 10:30. There are bathrooms available at this stop.

**Second Break:** Brevard College, bathrooms available. Bring a lunch.

**Finish:** Around 2 PM.

This event is hosted / cross-posted with the Society of American Pilgrims on the Camino, WNC/Asheville Chapter. The American Pilgrims provide education and training for people who want to walk the Camino de Santiago in Spain.
If you are unfamiliar with the Camino, here are a few links to learn more:
[American Pilgrims on the Camino](https://americanpilgrims.org/iwpmap_directory/western-north-carolina/)
[Stingy Nomads Camino](https://stingynomads.com/camino-de-santiago-walking-guide/)
**Monthly Bulletin - WNC Chapter - May 2026** [https://share.google/ljn28ijZqzfzw3qnE](https://share.google/ljn28ijZqzfzw3qnE)

**Scenic Asheville Series:** This hike counts as a Wildcard substitute on my Scenic Asheville Series. There are 9 [hikes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11ewlUM9OV8I4npc1cNNsSYOnXI0QPw2isAleXdFzEbI/edit?usp=drivesdk) in the series; hike them all and receive an [attractive badge](https://docs.google.com/drawings/d/1goXUXfzUBqhB4_UeCxodlk4ZPeCCgqZrWK2EUJvk_vI/edit) for your backpack. Check your status [HERE](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1XUm-X1_OhxKIi8JU5rhjsW37cAl4yYx8yB_NEjjI5Lk/edit?gid=0#gid=0).

**Guests:** For this hike, there are no guest restrictions. Bring them with you.

The organizer of this trip is a volunteer and not a professional guide. The function of the organizer is only to organize this trip. title: The Art of Presence: Meditation and Reflection in the Museum
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Step into the Museum’s galleries before the doors open for a quiet and contemplative morning of meditation, mindful walking, and reflection. This guided experience invites participants to slow down, settle the nervous system, and explore the Museum as a place of sanctuary, spaciousness, and renewal. 
The session will begin with a brief seated meditation, followed by a walking meditation through selected exhibits. Along the way, participants will pause with gentle mindfulness prompts designed to support personal reflection, embodied awareness, and a deeper connection with the artwork. Rather than offering art historical interpretation, the experience encourages each participant to notice what arises within them through presence, stillness, and mindful seeing. The group will honor noble silence throughout much of the session with occasional opportunities for brief reflection and sharing. No previous meditation experience is needed. 
Join Joshua on 8/22, 10/3, 11/7, and 12/5. 
Joshua Canter is a mindfulness meditation teacher and the founder of True Nature Travels and Education, an Asheville-based organization that has offered transformative retreats and educational experiences around the world for more than 20 years. He holds a master’s degree in Contemplative Psychology and is passionate about making mindfulness accessible, grounded, and relevant to everyday life. 
Purchase Tickets 
Please enter through the Staff Entrance to the left of the building.

title: Methods of Teaching Environmental Education Workshop, NC EE Criteria I
description:
Methods of Teaching Environmental Education Workshop, NC EE Criteria I
with Michelle Pearce 
4 hours of online self-guided online learning and 
In-person Saturday, December 5  |  10 am – 4 pm 
Register Here!
The Methods of Teaching EE (MOTEE) workshop helps practitioners create inclusive and age-appropriate learning experiences, gain group management skills, practice teaching methods to promote inquiry, and gain skills in designing objectives, lessons, and assessments for EE programs using NC Essential Standards as a foundation. This will be a hybrid workshop, with 4 hours of online, self-guided learning, in addition to a 6 hour in person session. Participants will receive 10 hours of Criteria 1 credit toward their NC EE Certification. 
This program will take place both in the classroom and outside following easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the part program time. 
Michelle Pearce has worked in Environmental Education since 2006. It was actually her first job right out of college, and she fell in love with it! Michelle has been a seasonal staff, Summer camp staff, county parks staff, a state employee, an adjunct professor, and now is currently serving as the Programming Lead for the Environmental Educators of North Carolina. She has a Bachelor’s degree in Biology with an emphasis in life science, and a Masters of Arts in Education with an emphasis in Science Education. She currently resides in Candler with her son and her leopard gecko.

title: Wild Pages: Creating Nature Zines
description:
Wild Pages: Creating Nature Zines
with Meg Worthington 
Saturday, December 5  |  1 – 4 pm 
Register Here!
Discover the creative world of zines while deepening your connection to the natural world around you. Zines are small, handmade publications that have long been used to share ideas, art, stories, and personal experiences. In this beginner-friendly workshop, participants will learn about the history and cultural significance of zines, explore examples of nature-focused zines, and create their own mini nature zine inspired by observations from the NC Arboretum. 
Through sketching, writing, collage, and simple book-folding techniques, participants will transform their observations into a unique publication they can take home. No artistic experience is necessary. This workshop is designed for adults of all skill levels and emphasizes curiosity, creativity, and careful observation. All materials will be provided, but feel free to bring in any personal art materials you may want to use. 
This class will take place primarily in a classroom, with a short portion taking place outside following easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for around 30 minutes. 
Meg Worthington (they/them) began teaching in Alaska while pursuing their Master’s degree in Outdoor and Environmental Education. While pursuing their degree they found a great sense of purpose in connecting students with the natural world and fostering a sense of curiosity and joy in learners of all ages. Meg’s experience working on a small educational farm in Palmer, Alaska helped to instill a keen interest in how we interact and cultivate our experiences within nature and our local communities. They are currently enjoying learning more about the local ecology of Western North Carolina and are excited to begin teaching classes as an Adult Education Specialist with the Adult Education Department at The NC Arboretum. Meg is also a local artist in the Asheville area, working with a variety of mediums including zines and collage to share and process the wide array of human emotions and what it means to be a soul. They love incorporating nature into their artwork and are always keen to learn new processes and artforms.

description:
Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.



Band Members include Dona Cavanagh, fiddle; Zena Rubin, banjo-uke; Maxine Herring, rhythm guitar; Hilary Dirlam, melody guitar; and Celia Millington-Wyckoff, bass.

title: Ecstatic Prom Fundraiser to Benefit AMC
description:
Asheville Movement Collective
Saturday, December 6th
Evening Dance Wave 6:00 pm \- 10:00 pm \| Warmup 6pm \| Opening Circle 6:30pm

Featuring Raffle, Photo Booth, and Refreshments!

Most of us remember prom, whether we went or not. Maybe it was a night you think of fondly, maybe it was awkward, or maybe you never went at all. Ecstatic Prom is a grown-up do-over, a chance to celebrate the dance that brings us all together and have some real fun doing it.

Ecstatic dance is a practice of moving freely to music, letting your body lead instead of following steps or a partner.

For nearly 25 years, the Asheville Movement Collective has created space for this practice in our city, growing into a community that now dances together every Friday night and Sunday morning. The dance can hold unexpected joy, space for grief to move, and moments of feeling at home in your body.

AMC is committed to keeping this dance open to everyone, regardless of financial means. We hold a No One Turned Away For Lack Of Funds policy, so reduced and free entry is always available to anyone who needs it. Beyond our weekly dances, we offer workshops and special events for the wider community, along with free childcare during 2nd Wave so parents can dance too.

That commitment is carried by our whole community, by every dancer whose weekly contribution keeps the dance going, and by events like Ecstatic Prom, an event-based fundraiser. If you're able to give more at checkout, it helps keep all of this open to everyone who wants to be part of it.

No dance experience needed.

Wear whatever feels celebratory and lets you move.

This is an alcohol and substance-free space.

description:

It's time for childlike wonder. Let's do a St. Nicholas Day walk in Waynesville and see the Christmas decorations.

Meet at 2:00 in front of Mast General Store, 63 N. Main St., Waynesville NC 28786. We will meet at the rocking chairs in front of the door to the shoe department.

The walk goes past public art, to Frog Level for a brief stop at Panacea Coffee Company, to Waynesville Middle School, through an interesting neighborhood, and back to the start point.

There are some hills, so some may want a walking pole (I will take 2); sneakers should be fine. Dogs are welcome. Strollers should be ok. Bring plenty of water and a protein snack. Dress appropriately for the weather. Consider a hat and, even though it is December, sunscreen.

Parking is easier a block to either side of Main Street. Mast General Store doesn't have a public restroom, but we can direct you to one nearby should you need it. There are one or two restrooms along the route.

title: Fantasy and Sci-Fi Silent Book Club
description:
Asheville Introverts
BOYB - Bring Your Own Book and rant or rave about your current Fantasy or Sci-fi titles!

**What is a Silent Book Club?**
Referred to as "Introvert's Happy Hour", Silent Book clubs allow readers to engage with each other without the commitment of reading a shared title. Community members gather in the same place, have some casual chit chat, and then read silently together. **This group will focus on Fantasy and Sci-Fi titles (subgenres & related genres are welcome!)**

**How does it work?**
For the first 15-30 mins we will gather, grab drinks and engage in introductions. Feel free to discuss your recent favorites, mention a title that lives in your head rent free, or ask for recommendations! The best part of the Silent Book Club is being able to talk shop with other readers!

Once settled in we will dedicate 45 minutes to silent reading. Your book can be traditional, ebook, or audiobook. Read at your own pace!

Afterwards we will go around show-and-tell style and share what we read with the group. We want to know what you're reading! Organic dialogue welcome!

title: New Moon Ceremony
description:
Senseful Soul’s Asheville Healing Community🧘🏻‍♀️🏳️‍🌈🪐🔮
Join us for a gathering to set new intentions and connect with the energy of the new moon.
Meet the New Moon in ceremony through astrology, Akashic soul journeying, ritual & embodied intention.
Approaching the threshold of a new lunar cycle with intentionality is a powerful choice that becomes even more amplified when done in community.

The New Moon offers a monthly portal to pause, listen inward, and consciously seed what you desire to cultivate in the cycle ahead. Gathering in ceremony creates the space to step outside the momentum of everyday life and meet that threshold with presence, allowing your intentions to be witnessed, embodied, and amplified within the collective.

Each New Moon also carries the unique energetic signature of the zodiac sign it moves through, offering different themes and invitations for your growth. By working intentionally with the astrology of each lunation, you can align your intentions with the energies already available to you and receive deeper clarity around what is ready to begin.

Each month, we gather at the Soul Sanctuary beneath the dark moon sky for an evening of astrology, soul journeying, ritual, and embodied intention.

**This month with the Sagittarius New Moon, we invite you to lift your gaze toward a larger horizon and reconnect with what makes you feel alive, expansive, and full of possibility.**

**Together, we’ll work with Sagittarius’ fiery medicine to clarify the truth and vision guiding our next chapter, strengthen our faith in where we’re being called, and plant intentions that ask us to move courageously toward it.**

**What to Expect**

* Guided drop-in meditation
* Astrological teaching + transmission
* Guided Akashic soul journey
* Reflection + intention setting
* Ceremonial fire offerings
* Closing embodiment + integration
* Sacred space for connection and community

No prior experience with astrology, meditation, or ceremonial practice is necessary. Simply come as you are.

**About Your Facilitators**
Alessandra Mary is a trained priestess, ceremonialist, and Akashic guide devoted to creating spaces where the sacred becomes something you can experience, embody, and weave into everyday life.

Jenn is a witch of the cosmos and astrologer who brings the language of the stars down to earth, illuminating the energetic patterns and possibilities available within each lunar cycle.

Together, Alessandra and Jenn weave the mystical and the embodied, the cosmic and the ceremonial, creating a space where you can not only understand the energy of the New Moon, but more importantly, experience it.

**What to Bring**
Our ceremony will primarily take place outside on the grass around the fire, with a large covered porch available as our rain plan. Please dress with the evening weather in mind.

**Be sure to bring:**

* Water bottle
* Journal + pen
* Comfortable clothing and layers appropriate for the weather
* Any sacred objects, crystals, talismans, or other items you would like to place on our collective altar and charge during the ceremony

Lawn blankets and meditation cushions will be provided, though you are very welcome to bring your own blanket, cushion, or camping chair if you’d prefer.

Come ready to slow down, listen deeply, sit beneath the dark moon, and lean into what is waiting to begin.

with Camille Daunno 
Tuesday, December 8  |  10am – 1pm 
Register Here!
Learn the art of needle felting with wool in this Snowman workshop. We will use foam spheres as the base for the snowman and colored wool in a pattern to create the design. No prior experience is necessary and this craft is very easy to learn. Get creative and add your own special touches to the project. In just 3 hours, you will leave with an adorable 10” snowman suitable to display or give as a gift. All materials are provided with the class. 
Camille Daunno is a retired Art Teacher with an undergraduate degree in Fine Art with graduate work in Textile Design. She worked in NYC as a designer for 10 years designing Fabric and wallpaper. Camille studied Art in NJ, NYC and Italy and studied Botanical Illustration and Painting at the NY Botanical Gardens with a certified instructor. She enjoys sharing her love of Botanical Art with her children and grandchildren.

title: Why Your Resolutions Fail by February (and How to Make This Year Different)
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
Every January we set big intentions, and by February most of them have quietly disappeared. It’s rarely about willpower. Usually two things get in the way: practical obstacles we haven’t planned for, and beliefs running underneath that pull us back to the old pattern.

In this 2-hour evening workshop, you’ll design the year you want and then take apart what’s been stopping you, at both levels.

**What we’ll do together:**

* Take a guided meditation into your ideal life, to get clear on what you really want.
* Map your goals across the six key areas of life
* Pick one goal and identify its practical obstacles, then turn them into simple, doable next steps
* Uncover any beliefs holding you back from your goal and keeping you stuck.
* Learn neuroplasticity-based tools you can use on your own to start rewiring that belief keeping you stuck.

You’ll leave with a clear goal, a realistic set of the first few baby steps and a worksheet to keep using all year.

**Who it’s for:** remote workers, freelancers, founders and anyone tired of starting the year strong and fading by spring.
**What to bring:** the goal you’re tired of failing at. Worksheets provided.
**Your host:** Jamie Leavitt is a certified coach, an RTT® hypnotherapist and the founder of The Inner Rewrite. After 25 years in corporate including 13 coaching leaders, she now helps high achievers get to the root of what keeps them stuck.
Spots are limited to 40.

**in 1860s Sicily, Don Fabrizio Corbera, Prince of Salina, remains skeptical and stoic as he faces civil war and his family's loss of wealth and status. The prince's favorite nephew, Tancredi, who opportunistically supports the unification efforts, marries Angelica, a beautiful woman from a lower social class, to secure his future. This marriage symbolizes the shifting social order and the decline of the aristocracy. As Don Fabrizio struggles to adapt, he retreats into his love of astronomy, finding solace in the unchanging stars while his world crumbles around him. Ultimately, he must decide to resist the forces of change or come to terms with them.**

**Giuseppe Tomasi di Lampedusa, the last in a line of Sicilian princes, drew inspiration from his own family's decline to write this novel in the 1950s. The dramatic sweep and richness of Lampedusa’s observation, his seamless intertwining of public and private worlds, and his sure grasp of human frailty imbue The Leopard with beauty and power.**

description:
Every atom in your body was forged in the belly of a dying star. The calcium in your bones, the iron in your blood, the carbon threading through every strand of your DNA — all of it cooked at temperatures beyond human language, scattered across the void, and reassembled over billions of years into something that walks into a bar on a Tuesday night and listens.

Sanders, Boyd, Page & Hall are four collections of stellar debris who have chosen to spend their brief window of consciousness making original music together. Not playing songs. Not running repertoire. Building something in real time from the raw material of attention, instinct, and decades of accumulated craft — compositions that didn't exist before these particular particles arranged themselves around instruments in this part...

title: Handmade Holiday: Weaving with Paper
description:
Handmade Holiday: Weaving with Paper
with Alyssa Sacora 
Tuesday, December 9  |  10am – 1pm 
Register Here!
Explore tabby and twill weaving techniques using a variety of papers. We’ll cover design concepts, material choices, and ways to add your own creative touch. A simple technique with endless possibilities, we’ll make several small pieces together that will serve as reference sampler for designing and weaving future projects. Woven paper pieces can be incorporated into wall art, cards, ornaments, vessels, and mixed media projects. All materials will be provided with this class. 
Alyssa Sacora is a crafts person exploring plant-based mediums in the form of papermaking, book arts, basketry and natural dyes. She finds inspiration by observing relationships in the wider world. To reduce her human footprint and encourage creative thinking, she primarily works with locally available and repurposed natural materials. Leaves, vines and bark from iris, daylily, kudzu, okra, tulip poplar and willow leaves are often combined with salvaged cotton fabrics to create her palette. Her artistic pursuits are directly related to her lifestyle choices with reciprocity and mindfulness as a guiding force. In addition to and in support of her craft, she tends a 3-acre homestead in Western North Carolina with her husband, Adam. They grow fruits and vegetables, medicinal herbs, and art plants. They use solar electric and solar thermal systems for electricity and heating, collect rain water and continuously look to design their space with sustainability in mind. Alyssa has taught for a variety of organizations in WNC and often utilizes an outside setting to help her students make the connection that we are nature and that our lives are intertwined with the plants, the soil, and the air around us.

title: Creative Alchemy: Winter Solstice - Dreaming Into the Dark
description:
Creative Alchemy: Winter Solstice – Dreaming Into the Dark
with Catherine Willows 
Thursday, December 10  |  10 am – 1 pm 
Register Here!
As we enter the cold and dark of winter, the Solstice invites us to slow down, turn inward, and listen to the quiet wisdom of the season. Gathering in the Arboretum, we’ll connect with the rhythms of Nature and the stillness, beauty, and mystery held within this time of year. 
Through guided reflection, intuitive painting, and the art-making experience, you’ll enter the portal of creativity—the realms of color, images, and inner wisdom beyond words. Resting into the stillness and magic of the season, we’ll make space for dreaming in the dark: bringing closure to the year while opening to the inklings, possibilities, and quiet stirrings of what may be revealed in the year ahead. 
No art experience is needed—only curiosity, an open heart, and a willingness to explore. All art supplies will be provided. 
Catherine Willows is a Registered Nurse, Certified Functional Medicine Health Coach, and Transformational Creativity Coach, and founder of Willows Coaching and Consulting. While holding sacred space, she guides adults in awakening their inner creativity — moving beyond the demands of daily life into greater flow, self-discovery, and joy through intuitive art-making processes. Catherine believes creativity and our connection to the natural world are deeply interwoven — both vital pillars of wellbeing, supporting nervous system regulation and inner equanimity, and together essential for living a meaningful, embodied life aligned with purpose and authentic expression.

title: Healthy Soil for Healthy Crops
description:
Healthy Soil for Healthy Crops
with Mark Dempsey 
Thursday, December 10  |  1 pm – 4 pm 
BREG – Core 
Register Here!
Come learn about how soil works and how to improve soil health. We will cover the basics of soil, the critical role of organic matter, how to sample soil and interpret a nutrient test, and what actions you can take to make your soil better. Drawing from research and on-farm experience, the class emphasizes practical, science-based strategies for improving soil health, reducing erosion, and building resilient farming systems. 
Mark Dempsey works with the Carolina Farm Stewardship Association as conservation specialist and soil health educator. His background includes more than 15 years of research and education in soil microbiology, no-till farming, cover crops, and sustainable agriculture systems. He teaches practical, science-based approaches to improving soil health, soil function, and long-term farm resilience.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Naturalist Walk & Talk
description:
Naturalist Walk and Talk
with Shane Myers 
Friday, December 11  |  1 – 3pm 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
Walk around the Arboretum with our staff naturalists and talk about what we see around us. We might see plants and animals, and evidence of them going about their lives in our backyard. Topics will be based on what we see and experience and whatever questions that come up, so every class has the potential to be quite different. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Shane Myers’ interest in nature began as a child with a love of dinosaurs. This quickly grew to include fossils, insects, and reptiles, and learning from the notes his grandparents kept of the birds that came to their feeders in Toledo, Ohio.  He has a Bachelors of Science in Wildlife Biology and did most of his undergraduate work on dragonflies and damselflies. He’s assisted in outreach and education for plant conservation groups, Odonata Groups, and various bird groups. Shane currently works for the Adult Education department at the NC Arboretum.

title: Plant Ecology
description:
Plant Ecology
with Alexandra Holland 
Friday, December 11  |  1 – 2:30pm 
BRN – Core  |  BREG – Elective 
Register Here!
Prerequisite: Beginning Botany 
In this class we’ll explore a variety of ways plants interact with one another and with other organisms from fungi to insects.  We’ll examine how plants compete and cooperate to survive in their environment. 
Alexandra Holland has a passion for getting people excited about the natural world through classes, hikes, and photography.  She graduated from Duke University and earned her master’s degree in botany from the University of Texas at Austin.  While in Texas, Alexandra managed the UTEX Culture Collection of Algae at UT Austin and volunteered with education programs at the Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center.  Upon moving to Asheville, she began volunteering with the NC Arboretum’s youth education programs.  In 2008 she was in the first class of students to be certified as Blue Ridge Naturalists.   Alexandra teaches botany classes at the NC Arboretum and leads nature hikes in Western NC for groups of all ages.

title: Winter Buds & Bark Tree ID
description:
Winter Buds & Bark Tree ID
with Lauren Lampley 
Friday, December 11  |  1 – 4pm 
BRN – Core |  BREG – Elective 
Register Here!
Ever wondered how you can identify a tree without its leaves? All tree species have different patterns of bark and leaf/flower buds that can be used to identify them even in winter time. In this program, we will look closely at the common trees around the NC Arboretum trails and point out specific characteristics of their buds and bark so you can identify them even without their leaves. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Lauren Lampley began her career at Grandfather Mountain Stewardship Foundation as a Park Naturalist which solidified Lauren’s interests in ecology and a passion for teaching others. She has led walks and hikes in a variety of subjects from Geology to Birding and especially enjoys learning and teaching about our local ecology. She currently works at the NC Arboretum as the Adult Education Coordinator managing all the programming hosted through the Adult Education Department.

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: J. Plank
description:
J. Plank (Jeff Plankenhorn) is a BC-based, internationally touring singer-songwriter and master of the lap steel guitar. Known for soulful vocals, dynamic stagecraft, and a sound that bridges roots, blues, and folk, he has spent decades captivating audiences across North America, Europe, and Japan. Plank is a highly respected musician recognized for his skill as a slide guitarist, songwriter, and vocalist, gaining acclaim both as a solo artist and as a sought-after session player. His style blends blues, folk, and roots into a sound that’s uniquely his own.



In 2025, he released The Bend, a stripped-down solo acoustic album recorded on the Texas coast, showcasing just his voice, lap steel, acoustic guitar, and piano. Later this year he will follow it with a high-energy roots rock album recorded in the Netherlands with the band The Southern Aces — a project that blends live-off-the-floor energy with wizardly guitar playing, innovative songwriting, and, most of all, deep groove.



Plank’s career includes collaborations with a wide range of artists, headline festival slots, and multiple Austin Music Award nominations for Musician of the Year, Best Guitarist, and a win for Best Misc. Instrument for “The Plank,” a hybrid lap steel guitar he designed himself. For him, music is about bringing people together — whether biker or drag queen, listener or dancer — to share in the joy and connection that only a great song can deliver...



Join him on his first performance at Jack of the Wood, along with a local Asheville band backing up every note. This is a show you shouldn't miss. Music 8:30-11:30pm $10 cover at the door.

title: Walking the NC Arboretum at the Willow Pond & Old Mill Trail
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Meet inside the Baker Visitor Center. Restrooms are available at the start point. We will start walking as soon as everyone has arrived.

The walk is a guided 5 KM trail. There are some moderate hills and stair climbing. A significant part of the route is on well-groomed trails with very few obstacles. Some people will want walking poles.

After exploring the Formal Gardens (Winter Lights will be up!), we will walk down Running Cedar Road and turn left on Bent Creek Road. We'll turn right on the Old Mill Trail and go out and back. Then we will take the Wesley Branch Trail and go right on the Lower Willow Pond Trail. After exploring the Willow Pond, we will follow the Upper Willow Pond Trail to the parking lot.

Dress for the weather; consider a hat and sunscreen (yes, even in December). Sneakers should be fine, unless it has rained recently. Be sure to bring **plenty of water** and a protein snack.

Dogs on leash are welcome but are not allowed in buildings or in the Bonsai Exhibit. Trail strollers should be ok.

The NC Arboretum does not have an admission fee, but they charge $25 per car parking fee (so pack as many people in your car as you can). We recommend the driver purchase the lowest level annual membership which includes free parking. (Of course, you may want a higher-level membership, your choice.) We walk at the Arboretum at least six times per year. A third option is to go to the comments section of this page and ask whether anyone would be willing to meet you and drive you into the Arboretum.

description:
Join us for an afternoon of music and art in the Museum. With a soundscape of piano music, we invite you to experience artwork in the galleries in a more emotional and sensory way. 
ABOUT THE MUSICIAN
Diego Vázquez is a Spanish pianist from Madrid now based in Asheville who views music as a way to understand and express emotions beyond words. He began playing at age four and developed a strong classical foundation, later expanding into pop and musical theater. After years of studying in Spain, he now pursues music independently in the United States, performing as a chapel pianist, choir member, and orchestra musician while also learning the organ. His cross-cultural journey shapes a deeply expressive style, with music focused on connection rather than perfection.

title: Exhibition on Screen | Van Gogh: Poets & Lovers
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Two hundred years after its opening and a century after acquiring its first Van Gogh artworks, the National Gallery, London is hosting the United Kingdom’s biggest ever Van Gogh exhibition. Van Gogh is not only one of the most beloved artists of all time, but perhaps the most misunderstood. 
This film is a chance to reexamine and better understand this iconic artist. Focusing on his unique creative process, Van Gogh: Poets & Lovers explores the artist’s years in the south of France, where he revolutionized his style. Van Gogh became consumed with a passion for storytelling in his art, turning the world around him into vibrant, idealized spaces and symbolic characters. 
Poets and lovers filled his imagination; everything he did in the south of France served this new obsession. In part, this is what caused his notorious breakdown, but it didn’t hold back his creativity as he created masterpiece after masterpiece. Explore one of art history’s most pivotal periods in this once-in-a-century show. Made in close collaboration with the National Gallery. 
Purchase Tickets

title: Game Night @ Archetype Brewing
description:
Asheville's Bored Game Geeks
tldr: \*\*We are at Archetype Brewing - West!\*\* Bring your favorite game(s) or learn a new one – members are always happy to teach! See you there and have a blast!

🎲🍻 **Welcome to the Game Night Extravaganza!** 🍻🎲

Calling all dice-rollers, card-shufflers, and strategy-curious adventurers! 🌟
Are weeknights feeling a tad mundane? Fear not! We’ve got the antidote: **Board Games, Brews, and Bliss**. 🍺🎮

🔥 **Our Mission:** To ignite laughter, forge alliances, and maybe—just maybe—unleash a few friendly rivalries & battle to the death! 🤪

No PhD in rulebooks required! Whether you’re a Settlers of Catan enthusiast or a Code Names solving ninja, or your first time touching a board game ***we will explain all the rules needed.*** 🏰🎉

Expect:

* **Beer on Tap**: Because rolling dice is better with a pint in hand.
* **Low Brainpower Required**: We’re all about fun, not Fermat’s Last Theorem.
* **Epic Showdowns**: Ticket to Ride routes, Splendor gem heists, and High stakes Camel Up.

Feel free to request any game you’d like to play or bring your own. So gather your guild, stack your resource cards, and let the games begin! May your laughter be loud, your moves be bold, and your victory dances be legendary. 🎭🎲
See you at the table! 🌟🍻

**Feel Free to bring your own games too!**

title: The Leadership Lounge
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
You want to do your best work every time. It's important to you, and you care about how you show up and what your team thinks of you.
Being present for ourselves is a significant challenge that often creates a gap. This gap represents the difference between the way we aspire to live and how we actually live. We choose to bridge this gap because it is the right thing to do.

Introducing a great way for new nomads to connect and discover important key takeaways for their lives. As a new Asheville Digital Nomad, where do you go if you don’t know many people?

You will participate in a discussion, yes! YOU, the audience, will be a part of a wonderful panel discussion. Whether you are a veteran or a newbie, come to **The Leadership Lounge**. You will get something out of this event and gain new insights to improve your outlook on how well you are settling into Asheville and Western North Carolina.

**The Leadership Lounge** presents a fabulous evening: **The Three Pillars.** This special occasion will introduce you to new actions to manage burnout and physiological changes, combining practicality with an intuitive desire for more fun.

title: Sapphic Book Club!  - December
description:
Queers to the Front!
Our book club read for December is *Bitterthorn* by Kat Dunn. A dark YA sapphic Gothic fantasy novel.

Blumwald is a town overshadowed by an ancient curse: in a sinister castle in the depths of the wild wood lives a monstrous Witch. Once a generation, she comes to claim a companion to return with her – never to be seen again. Now that time is drawing near once more...

Mina, daughter of the duke, is grieving and lonely. She has lost all hope of any future for herself in Blumwald. So when the Witch demands her next companion, Mina offers herself up – though she has no idea what fate awaits her. Stranded with her darkly alluring captor, the mystery of what happened to the previous companions draws Mina into the heart of a terrifying secret that could save her life, or end it.

The calcium in your bones, the iron in your blood, the carbon threading through every strand of your DNA — all of it cooked at temperatures beyond human language, scattered across the void, and reassembled over billions of years into something that walks into a bar on a Tuesday night and listens.

Sanders, Boyd, Page & Hall are four collections of stellar debris who have chosen to spend their brief window of consciousness making original music together. Not playing songs. Not running repertoire. Building something in real time from the raw material of attention, instinct, and decades of accumulated craft — compositions that didn't exist before these particular particles arranged themselves around instruments in this part...

title: Omni Grove Park Inn & Spa /Annual National Gingerbread House Competition ~ FREE!
description:
Senior Singles Fun Bunch
**The National Gingerbread House Competition is a nationally recognized competition and display at the Omni Grove Park Inn & Spa. Admission is FREE. The display of gingerbread houses features whimsical and elaborate handmade gingerbread houses of every size, shape, complexity, and theme. A must-see! You will see everything from rustic cabins to elaborate castles — all built from edible materials and made of at least 75% gingerbread. Contestants from all over the country submit their creations from across four age categories ~ adult, teen, youth, and child.**

**Besides seeing the gingerbread houses enjoy the enormous fireplaces, dozens of decorated Christmas trees with different themes, and the historic beauty of the Grove Park Inn. Also, treat yourself to their homemade hot chocolate or a hot toddy from the bar. That’s what I plan on doing! I want a hot-buttered rum and to sit in one of the rocking chairs in front of one of those huge fireplaces! Ahhhh! 🔥 🍹Come join me!**

**To read more about all that is offered at the Inn google The National Gingerbread House Competition for there are many articles and beautiful photos of gingerbread houses. You can also go to: www.omnihotels.com.**

**PUBLIC VIEWING:** **👀** **Unless you’re a registered guest of the hotel the gingerbread houses can only be viewed Monday-Thursday. That’s why our meetup is not scheduled for the weekend.**

**PETS: 🐶** **Only pets of registered guests are allowed.**

**PARKING: 🅿️** **Admission is free, but parking certainly isn’t!**
**Valet: $40 for day parking.**
**Self-parking: $30 for day parking.**
**The proceeds from parking benefits local non-profits.**

**CARPOOLING: 🚗** **I encourage carpooling due to the price of parking. If you’re willing to do so please comment in the comment section for this meetup event. Please leave contact info.**

**DAWN/CARPOOLING: 🚙** **Dawn has a nice-size Flex Ford and can accept five passengers. The first five to respond get the seats! We will be doing the valet parking for $40 plus tip. Split seven ways (that includes Dawn & me) it will be about $7-$8 per person. Beats paying the whole $40!**
**If you wish to carpool with Dawn please text me (please no phone calls for I work and my phone will be off) or email me. All others who wish to let others ride with them please make a comment in the comment section. My contact information is at bottom.**
**For those riding with Dawn we will be meeting up at IHOP Restaurant on Airport Rd. Please read the separate meetup event for IHOP. Dawn & I will be having breakfast there prior to leaving for the Grove Park Inn. Come join us or just come before we depart (Again, for details please look at the separate meetup event for IHOP). I know this is a lot of information so please text or email me with any questions.**

**DINING:🍴I tried to get dining at the Inn, but for a large group they now require you to pay in advance for everyone with only one credit card. No can do. I also wanted the Sunset Terrace, but they close in early November. Several of the restaurants are seasonal. But if you want something to eat while there they do serve food at their many on-site bars & restaurants (that are not seasonal).**

**Again, please text or email me (info. below) if you wish to carpool (first come, first serve) with Dawn or if you simply have some questions.**

**WHERE TO MEET ME:** **For those NOT carpooling with Dawn I will meet you inside the main entrance/lobby of the Inn at 11:30 AM. I’ll be in the area of one of the two huge fireplaces ~ preferably the one where I can get a rocker in front of the fireplace. 🔥 Text or call me if you can’t find me. (828)699-8180. Hope to see you there! Tis the season! 🎄 🎄🎄**

**QUESTIONS?**
**Shae ~ (828)699-8180**

title: Weekly Critique
description:
AVL Writers
This is the standing weekly critique. Bring anything new you're working on to share with the group. If you don't have a project to share, you are most welcome to attend, discuss, and get inspired.

For our group discussion, please bring at least 8-10 printed copies of your piece. That way, we can all read through each other's work and provide feedback.

Sharing our creative efforts is an important part of the writing process. I'm really looking forward to reading what you've been working on. Don't worry if it's still a rough draft.

If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.

If you would like to join our group email list for updates regarding contests, events, and more [you can sign up on our website](https://avlwriters.com/).

title: Value Studies: Member Preview
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
As a valued Museum Member, we invite you to join us for the exclusive preview of our newest exhibition—Value Studies: Artmaking and Worldmaking at Black Mountain College. 
4–5pm | Upper-Level Members 
Register Here 
5–7pm | All Members 
Register Here 
About the Exhibition
Value Studies brings together highlights from the Museum’s permanent collection and key loans to consider Black Mountain College (1933–1957) as a site where students and faculty modeled new ways of living, learning, and relating to one another. This practice of imagining new worlds, and enacting them collectively, arose during a moment of profound uncertainty in American history that prompted many people to rethink the values, institutions, and relationships ordering their everyday lives—and offered the possibility of creating alternative futures. 
The exhibition’s three sections—Color Studies, Material Studies, and Figure Studies—use foundational classroom exercises as conceptual frameworks for exploring the BMC community’s ethics in action, revealing the values at the heart of their vision for the future. Featuring significant works by Anni & Josef Albers, Ruth Asawa, Elaine & Willem de Kooning, Gwendolyn Knight & Jacob Lawrence, and Robert Rauschenberg, among many others, Value Studies explores the new worlds being made at Black Mountain College—offering viewers the opportunity to consider how they themselves might question, envision, and actively shape the world around them. 
This exhibition is supported by the National Endowment for the Arts. 
Please note:
Exhibition Previews are reserved for current Museum Members; please only register Members included in your membership. 
Join the fun—Become a Member today!

location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Every Third Thursday, the Museum comes alive with an evening filled with music, tours, art making, special cocktails in our rooftop café, and more! 
Enjoy live music from the Jason DeCristofaro Jazz Trio featuring Jason DeCristofaro, Bob Songster and Andy Applegate.  For this performance, the trio will be performing special Christmas and holiday selections.   
Dr. Jason DeCristofaro an active music educator, multi-instrumentalist and composer/arranger based in Asheville, NC.  He is an Assistant Professor of Music and the Chair of the Music Department at Warren Wilson College, where he also acts as Director of the Kittredge Arts Center.  Jason’s classical and jazz music has been performed internationally and throughout the United States, and his compositions are published with C. Alan, Per-Mus and Tapspace.   The winner of the 2011 Yamaha/Percussive Arts Society Terry Gibbs Competition (an international competition for jazz vibraphonists), Jason has performed on national and global stages with Randy Brecker, Dr. Sam Waymon (Nina Simone’s brother), Jocelyn Gould, and Sharel Cassity.   
Andy Applegate is a jazz drummer and vibraphonist currently based in Asheville, NC. Andy obtained his Bachelor of Music degree in Jazz commercial music from Temple University in Philadelphia. After years on the Philly scene he ended up in Asheville then moved to Los Angeles for a decade. While in LA, he worked with many well-known jazz groups including the Teddy Bang jazz trio, guitarist Hideaki Tokunaga, the LA Love band and the Flamenco Souls latin jazz band. In 2024 Andy returned to Asheville and has been immersed in the jazz and diverse music scene there.
