title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: The Nature Boys
description:
Hailing from the Appalachian musical stronghold of Asheville, NC, The Nature Boys are coming in hot with their brand of bluegrass. As veterans of the acoustic music scene, they are combining a deep love of traditional string band music with a refreshing catalog of original songs, dazzling fans with a certain je ne sais quoi that is both genuine and relatable. 



Formed in the summer of 2025, long time friends Jack, Jesse, and Nick found themselves once again living in the same town and ready to start a new musical project. These three had spent years touring across the world, often but not always in the same group. With a shared love of music, humor, and brotherhood, The Nature Boys was born in a way that can only be described as natural. Soon after getting the wheels rolling, they enlisted Asheville aces Coop and Korey, now forming one of Asheville’s premier 5-piece bluegrass bands, The Nature Boys.



The band is currently performing regionally and is recording their debut album, to be released in late 2026. Music from 8:30-11:30pm, $10 cover at the door.

title: Walk 10 KM on the Pickens Doodle Trail from Pickens SC
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
The Pickens SC trailhead for the Doodle Trail is at 409 E. Cedar Rock Street, Pickens SC 29671. The trail is a 7.5 mile rails-to-trails partnership between the City of Easley and the City of Pickens. We will be start at the Pickens trailhead, walk 3 miles, and return to the start point. We will be sharing the trail with bikers, runners, and rollerbladers.

Local residents nicknamed the railroad the "Pickens Doodle" line, because the freight engine could not be turned around and had to run backwards from Easley to Pickens, looking like a doodlebug.

Pickens Doodle Park, where the trailhead is located, includes restroom facilities, a railroad depot museum, a pavilion, benches, bike racks, and a train-themed playground.

Dress for the weather. You probably won't need a walking stick (although I plan to take one). Bring plenty of water and a protein snack. Consider a hat and sunscreen (yes, even though it is December). Wheelchairs and strollers should have no problem. Dogs are welcome (though you must clean up after your pet).

This is a new walk for me. Come and help me explore an interesting new location.

title: Forest Bathing Retreat: Winter Solstice Wander
description:
Forest Bathing Retreat: Winter Solstice Wander
with Asheville Wellness Tours 
Saturday, December 19  |  1:30 – 4:30pm 
Register Here!
Discover the wisdom of the Winter Solstice in the Blue Ridge Mountains during this immersive afternoon nature connection retreat. A gentle invitational experience to enliven your senses, slow down the hectic pace, quiet your weary mind, and linger in liminality. Together, we will explore natural pathways to equanimity that will help us navigate life’s ups and downs and the holiday season. 
Your guide, Christa Hebal, will lead you on a peaceful saunter through the fall forest, weaving mindfulness, breathwork, forest bathing and nature therapy together for a restorative afternoon on some of the trails less traveled at the North Carolina Arboretum. We’ll celebrate the experience in community, enjoying a special wild-foraged tea ceremony and snacks. Bring an open mind and an open heart. All are welcome. Presented through Adult & Continuing Education Programs in collaboration with Asheville Wellness Tours. 
Christa Hebal is a certified Nature and Forest Therapy Guide by the Association of Nature and Forest Therapy. Born and raised in the mountains of northeast Tennessee, she has lived in Asheville for 24 years. Christa has an adventurous heart, and loves to help others encounter wholeness through embodiment and nature connection practices. She has had a professional bodywork practice for 18 years as a nationally certified Massage Therapist, and is also a practitioner of Ortho-Bionomy®, Usui Reiki Master, Certified Pediatric Massage Therapist, Clinical Aromatherapist, and Certified Traditional Herbalist. She is also certified in CPR and Wilderness First Aid.

Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.

title: Gaming Night @ Noble Cider
description:
Asheville's Bored Game Geeks
Roll the dice and pour a glass! 🎲🍎

Gaming Night is back at Noble Cider! Join us every other Tuesday for a night of tabletop tactics, card-shuffling chaos, and great company. Whether you’re a seasoned strategist or you still think a "meeple" is a type of small fruit, you’re welcome at our table.

* **No Experience? No Problem:** We’re all about community. We’ll help you learn the ropes of a new game or cheer you on while you figure it out.
* **The Library:** We have a solid stash of games ready to play—from quick party favorites to deeper strategy titles.
* **Bring Your Favorites:** Have a game gathering dust on your shelf? Bring it along! We love seeing what the community is playing.
* **The Vibe:** High-quality cider, cozy atmosphere, and just the right amount of competitive spirit.

**Feel Free to bring your own games too!**

title: Weekly Critique
description:
AVL Writers
This is the standing weekly critique. Bring anything new you're working on to share with the group. If you don't have a project to share, you are most welcome to attend, discuss, and get inspired.

For our group discussion, please bring at least 8-10 printed copies of your piece. That way, we can all read through each other's work and provide feedback.

Sharing our creative efforts is an important part of the writing process. I'm really looking forward to reading what you've been working on. Don't worry if it's still a rough draft.

If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.

If you would like to join our group email list for updates regarding contests, events, and more [you can sign up on our website](https://avlwriters.com/).

RIGHT out of OLR parking lot

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

description:

Led by Founding teacher Ronya Banks or AIM Facilitator Wallace Bohanan, our Thursday evening group meditation sessions will continue to consist of a guided meditation (30 minutes), a few-minute break, a dharma talk by the teacher (30 minutes), and then Q & A/Discussion (30 minutes).

title: NOBODY'S DARLING STRING BAND
description:
Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.



Band Members include Dona Cavanagh, fiddle; Zena Rubin, banjo-uke; Maxine Herring, rhythm guitar; Hilary Dirlam, melody guitar; and Celia Millington-Wyckoff, bass.



The five women comprising Nobody’s Darling each have a long history of playing old-time music. Individually they have played in many other bands through the years, including The Carolina Oldtimers, The Pegtwisters, The Zuma House Band, Too Hot To Cook, The Luke Smathers Mountain Swing Band, Honey Holler, and The Carolina Chick Peas.



Stop in to enjoy the music and an afternoon libation or two, perhaps with an early supper or light bite . . . and don't forget your dancing shoes!

tldr: \*\*We are at Archetype Brewing - West!\*\* Bring your favorite game(s) or learn a new one – members are always happy to teach! See you there and have a blast!

🎲🍻 **Welcome to the Game Night Extravaganza!** 🍻🎲

Calling all dice-rollers, card-shufflers, and strategy-curious adventurers! 🌟
Are weeknights feeling a tad mundane? Fear not! We’ve got the antidote: **Board Games, Brews, and Bliss**. 🍺🎮

🔥 **Our Mission:** To ignite laughter, forge alliances, and maybe—just maybe—unleash a few friendly rivalries & battle to the death! 🤪

No PhD in rulebooks required! Whether you’re a Settlers of Catan enthusiast or a Code Names solving ninja, or your first time touching a board game ***we will explain all the rules needed.*** 🏰🎉

Expect:

* **Beer on Tap**: Because rolling dice is better with a pint in hand.
* **Low Brainpower Required**: We’re all about fun, not Fermat’s Last Theorem.

title: OLD-TIME JAM
description:
The roots of Appalachian old-time music stretch far across the Atlantic and we're proud to honor and showcase that legacy at Jack of the Wood Pub with our long-running Old-Time Jam sessions — every Wednesday starting at 5pm! Recently recommended by Rolling Stone for "those looking for an organic, participatory [music] experience" in Asheville, the Old-Time Jam is one of several weekly traditional jam sessions hosted at JACK.



Our cozy Celtic pub is the perfect spot downtown to take in some of the region's finest traditional acoustic musicians playing "in the round" while you enjoy a pint or two and the best pub fare in town!
source: Jack of the Wood, Where Y'at AVL Music

title: Weekly Critique
description:
AVL Writers
This is the standing weekly critique. Bring anything new you're working on to share with the group. If you don't have a project to share, you are most welcome to attend, discuss, and get inspired.

For our group discussion, please bring at least 8-10 printed copies of your piece. That way, we can all read through each other's work and provide feedback.

Sharing our creative efforts is an important part of the writing process. I'm really looking forward to reading what you've been working on. Don't worry if it's still a rough draft.

If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.

If you would like to join our group email list for updates regarding contests, events, and more [you can sign up on our website](https://avlwriters.com/).

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: New Year’s Day Polar Bear  Plunge & Centennial Celebration ~ Lake Lure, N.C.
description:
Senior Singles Fun Bunch
**Let’s start the New Year 2027 🥳 off by going to the Polar Plunge at Lake Lure! And better yet, why not register to take the plunge?! I will cheer you on for there’s no way you’re getting me into that cold water! Brrrrr! 🧊 💦 But I would love to see you do it!! 😂 This will be a fun event!! So come join me!! There will be bonfires, 🔥 hot chocolate, cookies, 🍪 music 🎵 and prizes for best costumes and for the youngest and oldest plunger! Fun! 🤩**

**A GOOD CAUSE: This annual New Year’s event in Lake Lure (except for the last couple of years due to the hurricane devastation) draws hundreds of people who jump into the lake to help raise money for local first responders.**

**This year it’s being promoted as the first event of the Hickory Nut Gorge Chamber’s centennial year with proceeds benefiting the Lake Lure Fire Department. 👨‍🚒👩‍🚒**

**REGISTER TO JUMP INTO THE LAKE:**
**Register after Thanksgiving in person at the Lake Lure Beach House. 2724 Memorial Highway, Lake Lure, N.C. between 10:30-11:30 AM. No online registration is available. Additional information at www.hickorynutchamber.org.**

**PETS: 🐶 No dogs allowed on the beach.**

**PARKING: 🅿️ I strongly suggest you come early to find a parking place.**

**WHERE TO FIND ME: I’ll try and be in the La Strada parking lot at 11:00 AM so we can meet up. I’ll have my colorful corgi bag on me as usual. Look at photos below to see my bag. You can text me or call me, too. (828)699-8180.**

**AFTER THE PLUNGE ~~**
**A BITE TO EAT: I plan on grabbing a bite to eat (after the plunge is over) at the La Strada Restaurant which is located right across the street from the beach. They do not take reservations. So come join me for a bite if you like. I have no idea what exact time I’ll be there though. It depends on how things go at the plunge ~~ so just look for me inside. Menu at www.lastradaatlakelure.com.**

**PARKING & PETS: 🅿️🐶 Usually there is ample parking at the restaurant, but with all of the activities it may be limited.**
**Pets are only allowed on the covered outdoor patio. The restaurant even provides a doggie menu! 🐶 Woof!**

**QUESTIONS/CONCERNS:**

title: NOBODY'S DARLING STRING BAND
description:
Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.



Band Members include Dona Cavanagh, fiddle; Zena Rubin, banjo-uke; Maxine Herring, rhythm guitar; Hilary Dirlam, melody guitar; and Celia Millington-Wyckoff, bass.



The five women comprising Nobody’s Darling each have a long history of playing old-time music. Individually they have played in many other bands through the years, including The Carolina Oldtimers, The Pegtwisters, The Zuma House Band, Too Hot To Cook, The Luke Smathers Mountain Swing Band, Honey Holler, and The Carolina Chick Peas.



Stop in to enjoy the music and an afternoon libation or two, perhaps with an early supper or light bite . . . and don't forget your dancing shoes!

title: Birding for Beginners
description:
Birding for Beginners
with Shane Myers 
Tuesday, January 5  |  9 – 10:30 am 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
Starting in the classroom, you will get a chance to learn best practices for using binoculars, try out spotting scopes, and look at different field guides. Later in class, we’ll move outside and practice observing birds around the buildings and core garden area. Bring your own binoculars but if you do not have a pair, we have some loaner binoculars available to use during the program. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Shane Myers’ interest in nature began as a child with a love of dinosaurs. This quickly grew to include fossils, insects, and reptiles, and learning from the notes his grandparents kept of the birds that came to their feeders in Toledo, Ohio.  He has a Bachelors of Science in Wildlife Biology and did most of his undergraduate work on dragonflies and damselflies. He’s assisted in outreach and education for plant conservation groups, Odonata Groups, and various bird groups. Shane currently works for the Adult Education department at the NC Arboretum.

title: Botanical Drawing for Beginners
description:
Botanical Drawing for Beginners
with Camille Daunno 
Four Sessions: 
Tuesdays, January 5, 12, 19, and 26 | 9:30 am – 12:30 pm 
Register Here!
Discover the fundamentals of botanical drawing in this welcoming beginner-level class. During this four-week series students will learn essential drawing techniques including contour drawing, line work, shading and texture. Through guided instruction and observation, students will build confidence in capturing the shapes, patterns, and details found in nature while developing their own artistic style. All materials are provided, and participants will leave with in-progress and completed works as well as new skills to continue their botanical drawing practice at home. 
Camille Daunno is a retired Art Teacher with an undergraduate degree in Fine Art with graduate work in Textile Design. She worked in NYC as a designer for 10 years designing Fabric and wallpaper. Camille studied Art in NJ, NYC and Italy and studied Botanical Illustration and Painting at the NY Botanical Gardens with a certified instructor. Her favorite audience to share her love of Botanical art with is her children and grandchildren.

title: Gaming Night @ Noble Cider
description:
Asheville's Bored Game Geeks
Roll the dice and pour a glass! 🎲🍎

Gaming Night is back at Noble Cider! Join us every other Tuesday for a night of tabletop tactics, card-shuffling chaos, and great company. Whether you’re a seasoned strategist or you still think a "meeple" is a type of small fruit, you’re welcome at our table.

### The Lowdown:

* **No Experience? No Problem:** We’re all about community. We’ll help you learn the ropes of a new game or cheer you on while you figure it out.

title: Envisioning the New Year with Creativity & Vision Board-Making
description:
Envisioning the New Year with Creativity & Vision Board-Making
with Catherine Willows 
Thursday, January 7  |  12 – 4 pm 
Register Here!
A new year opens like a blank canvas, inviting us to awaken our imagination and explore what we wish to create, experience, and welcome into our lives. The first New Moon following Winter Solstice offers a beautiful moment for renewal, fresh perspective, and envisioning new possibilities. As the returning light begins to illuminate the winter landscape, we, too, can begin to see what is ready to emerge. Gathering at the Arboretum, we’ll connect with the rhythms of Nature and the Creative Life Force through guided reflection and intuitive art-making. Beyond traditional goal-setting or vision boarding, this is an invitation to open a creative portal into the possibilities of a new cycle. Through collage, painting, color, imagery, symbols, and words, you’ll create a personal vision board expressing the inspiration and possibilities drawing you forward. No art experience is needed—just curiosity, an open heart, and a willingness to explore. 
Art supplies will be provided. Please bring magazines or images to cut and paste, along with a journal. 
Catherine Willows is a Registered Nurse, Certified Functional Medicine Health Coach, and Transformational Creativity Coach, and founder of Willows Coaching and Consulting. While holding sacred space, she guides adults in awakening their inner creativity — moving beyond the demands of daily life into greater flow, self-discovery, and joy through intuitive art-making processes. 
Catherine believes creativity and our connection to the natural world are deeply interwoven — both vital pillars of wellbeing, supporting nervous system regulation and inner equanimity, and together essential for living a meaningful, embodied life aligned with purpose and authentic expression.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Listening through the Seasons: Introduction to Soundscapes
description:
Listening through the Seasons: Introduction to Soundscapes
with Meg Worthington 
Friday, January 8 | 1 – 3:30 pm 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
How does the Arboretum sound in winter? What can we learn by listening closely? 
Join us as we launch a yearlong exploration of the NC Arboretum’s changing soundscape. In this introductory session, participants will discover the field of soundscape ecology, learn how scientists use sound to study ecosystems, and practice techniques for deep listening and observation. Together, we’ll visit our first listening station, collect baseline observations, and begin documenting the sounds of winter. 
Listening Through the Seasons is a yearlong community science and soundscape ecology project at the NC Arboretum. Participants will help document the changing sounds of the Arboretum throughout the year while learning about ecology, biodiversity, and the art of deep listening. Through field observations, sound recording, and guided activities, we’ll create a seasonal acoustic portrait of the Arboretum and contribute to an ongoing research project exploring how natural soundscapes change over time. 
This program includes instruction both inside a classroom and outside following easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for at least half of the class. 
 Meg Worthington (they/them) is an educator, artist, and lifelong learner whose work is rooted in curiosity, creativity, and connection to the natural world. They began teaching in Alaska while earning a Master’s degree in Outdoor and Environmental Education, where they discovered a passion for creating meaningful experiences that inspire wonder and exploration. Working on a small educational farm in Palmer, Alaska, deepened Meg’s appreciation for the relationships between people, place, and community. Today, they are enjoying the opportunity to learn more about the unique ecology of Western North Carolina and are excited to teach as an Adult Education Specialist at The NC Arboretum. As a local Asheville artist, Meg creates zines, collages, and mixed-media works that explore human emotion, personal growth, and our search for meaning. Nature is a constant source of inspiration in their creative practice, and they delight in experimenting with new materials, techniques, and art forms.

description:
Asheville's Bored Game Geeks
tldr: \*\*We are at Archetype Brewing - West!\*\* Bring your favorite game(s) or learn a new one – members are always happy to teach! See you there and have a blast!

🎲🍻 **Welcome to the Game Night Extravaganza!** 🍻🎲

Calling all dice-rollers, card-shufflers, and strategy-curious adventurers! 🌟
Are weeknights feeling a tad mundane? Fear not! We’ve got the antidote: **Board Games, Brews, and Bliss**. 🍺🎮

🔥 **Our Mission:** To ignite laughter, forge alliances, and maybe—just maybe—unleash a few friendly rivalries & battle to the death! 🤪

No PhD in rulebooks required! Whether you’re a Settlers of Catan enthusiast or a Code Names solving ninja, or your first time touching a board game ***we will explain all the rules needed.*** 🏰🎉

Expect:

* **Beer on Tap**: Because rolling dice is better with a pint in hand.
* **Low Brainpower Required**: We’re all about fun, not Fermat’s Last Theorem.
* **Epic Showdowns**: Ticket to Ride routes, Splendor gem heists, and High stakes Camel Up.

Feel free to request any game you’d like to play or bring your own. So gather your guild, stack your resource cards, and let the games begin! May your laughter be loud, your moves be bold, and your victory dances be legendary. 🎭🎲
See you at the table! 🌟🍻

**Feel Free to bring your own games too!**

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Evening Group Meditation IN-PERSON or ONLINE
description:
Asheville Meditation Meetup Group
Led by Founding teacher Ronya Banks or AIM Facilitator Wallace Bohanan, our Thursday evening group meditation sessions will continue to consist of a guided meditation (30 minutes), a few-minute break, a dharma talk by the teacher (30 minutes), and then Q & A/Discussion (30 minutes).

Meditation instructions will be given for beginners.

The session begins promptly at 7:00 pm. If online, please mute your audio during the guided meditation and talk.

Location

MindSpring Building
966 Tunnel Road, Asheville, NC 28805

Please Donate ($10 Suggested)

We need your generosity now more than ever before. Please hit the Donate Button to your right and donate whatever you can afford. Or become one of our monthly sustaining donars. (The suggested minimum donation is $10, but no one is turned away for lack of funds.)

Group Meditation Guidelines

* Arrive several minutes early. You are welcome to greet others before we start.
* Turn off your cell phones and other beeping devices.
* Sit in a comfortable position, chairs are provided, bring your own cushions, blankets, or props.
* If on zoom, please mute yourself during guided meditation, and talk, and then unmute yourself to share during the discussion.

title: Gaming Night @ Noble Cider
description:
Asheville's Bored Game Geeks
Roll the dice and pour a glass! 🎲🍎

Gaming Night is back at Noble Cider! Join us every other Tuesday for a night of tabletop tactics, card-shuffling chaos, and great company. Whether you’re a seasoned strategist or you still think a "meeple" is a type of small fruit, you’re welcome at our table.

### The Lowdown:

* **No Experience? No Problem:** We’re all about community. We’ll help you learn the ropes of a new game or cheer you on while you figure it out.
* **The Library:** We have a solid stash of games ready to play—from quick party favorites to deeper strategy titles.
* **Bring Your Favorites:** Have a game gathering dust on your shelf? Bring it along! We love seeing what the community is playing.
* **The Vibe:** High-quality cider, cozy atmosphere, and just the right amount of competitive spirit.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: The Storehouse Food Pantry
location: 1049 Spartanburg Hwy, Hendersonville, NC 28739, USA
description:
Selection of fresh and non-perishable food items for eligible Henderson County residents.

Get Help | The Storehouse of Henderson County https://storehouseonline.org/get-help


What to Expect & Bring

Eligibility: Assistance is available to residents of Henderson County facing food insecurity.

What to Bring: Valid photo ID and proof of Henderson County residency (like a recent utility bill, lease agreement, or official mail with your current address).

No appointment necessary. You can visit the pantry during regular operating hours. Service is generally provided on a first-come, first-served basis.

The Process: Volunteers will greet you, help you with a brief registration, and provide you with a selection of fresh and non-perishable food items.

What to Expect & Bring

Eligibility: Assistance is available to residents of Henderson County facing food insecurity.

What to Bring: Valid photo ID and proof of Henderson County residency (like a recent utility bill, lease agreement, or official mail with your current address).

No appointment necessary. You can visit the pantry during regular operating hours. Service is generally provided on a first-come, first-served basis.

The Process: Volunteers will greet you, help you with a brief registration, and provide you with a selection of fresh and non-perishable food items.

What to Expect & Bring

Eligibility: Assistance is available to residents of Henderson County facing food insecurity.

What to Bring: Valid photo ID and proof of Henderson County residency (like a recent utility bill, lease agreement, or official mail with your current address).

No appointment necessary. You can visit the pantry during regular operating hours. Service is generally provided on a first-come, first-served basis.

The Process: Volunteers will greet you, help you with a brief registration, and provide you with a selection of fresh and non-perishable food items.

title: Re-Entry Simulation
location: Upper Fellowhip Hall
description:
A re-entry simulation places participants in the role of a “returning citizen” and asks them to complete weekly tasks—such as reporting to probation, securing housing, finding employment, accessing transportation, obtaining IDs, managing fines, and meeting basic needs. Stations represent real-world agencies and services, and participants quickly experience how limited time, financial constraints, bureaucratic hurdles, and strict supervision requirements create overwhelming barriers.

The simulation demonstrates how easily people can fall out of compliance, not because of unwillingness, but because the system is complex, inflexible, and often impossible to navigate without support. It builds empathy, deepens understanding of structural barriers, and highlights the importance of re-entry support, community resources, and fair supervision practices.
